confirmed.title: agent-serve registers research executor with nil Fetcher — every research task fails at runtime
confirmed.evidence: buildExecutorRegistry(): `executor.TaskResearch: executor.NewResearchExecutor(nil)`. The constructor contract (internal/executor/research.go:127-129) says "Fetcher must not be nil; the caller decides between HTTPFetcher (production) and StubFetcher (tests)", and Execute (research.go:167) returns `fmt.Errorf("research executor: no Fetcher configured")` when nil. agentserve/server.go:241 advertises the type as a capability and server.go:363 calls ex.Execute, so every research task submitted over agent-serve errors. The sibling CLI path wires a real fetcher (cmd/r1/research_cmd.go:77), proving the intended wiring exists.
confirmed.fix: In cmd/r1/agent_serve_cmd.go buildExecutorRegistry (line 461), replace executor.NewResearchExecutor(nil) with executor.NewResearchExecutor(research.NewHTTPFetcher()) and add the "github.com/RelayOne/r1/internal/research" import — identical wiring to cmd/r1/research_cmd.go:72-77. NewHTTPFetcher (internal/research/fetch.go:61-78) is self-contained with env-driven config (R1_RESEARCH_ALLOWLIST, R1_RESEARCH_REQUIRE_TLS), so no operator dependencies. Add a regression test asserting buildExecutorRegistry's TaskResearch executor has a non-nil Fetcher (e.g., cast to *executor.ResearchExecutor and check ex.Fetcher != nil), so the nil wiring can never silently return.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified end-to-end at HEAD. cmd/r1/agent_serve_cmd.go:461 registers executor.NewResearchExecutor(nil); the registry is passed unmodified into agentserve.Config (line 57) and internal/agentserve/server.go:270/363 dispatches POST /api/task directly to ex.Execute. internal/executor/research.go:164-167 returns "research executor: no Fetcher configured" as the first statement of Execute when Fetcher is nil, so no code path escapes it. With the default empty --caps ("empty = all registered", agent_serve_cmd.go:142), server.go:240-243 advertises "research" from the Executors map on GET /api/capabilities and via TrustPlane registration, and server.go:377-380 marks every submitted research task "failed". Not intentional: the registry comment (lines 452-453) claims "Every wired executor from Tasks 20-22 is registered" and the constructor contract (research.go:126-129) says "Fetcher must not be nil"; this is the only nil-Fetcher call site in the repo — all others use StubFetcher (tests) or a real fetcher (cmd/r1/research_cmd.go:64-77). CI never catches it because tests use StubFetcher. Concrete consequence: every research task submitted to the hireable-agent HTTP facade fails at runtime, and with --trustplane-register the resulting failed terminal transitions trigger Dispute settlements for a capability the agent advertised.

confirmed.title: r1-coord-api /v1/license/verify: dead EOF guard plus accepts any 8+ char key as valid on a public prod endpoint
confirmed.evidence: `if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, fmt.Errorf("EOF"))` — errors.Is against a freshly-allocated fmt.Errorf can never match, so empty-body requests 400 instead of the intended EOF fall-through (the telemetry handler at :196 correctly uses io.EOF). And the endpoint's whole 'verification' is `valid := len(req.Key) >= 8` (:181) returning reason "well-formed key" — a licensing stub live on an --allow-unauthenticated prod service.
confirmed.fix: In services/r1-coord-api/main.go:177 replace `!errors.Is(err, fmt.Errorf("EOF"))` with `!errors.Is(err, io.EOF)` (matching main.go:196; io is already imported). Make the stub honest: change the reason strings at main.go:185 to state shape-check-only (e.g. "shape check only (stub, no key store): key >= 8 chars" / "key shorter than 8 chars") or add a "mode":"shape-check" field, and fix the header doc at main.go:7 to say "valid when key length >= 8; shape check only, no key store" instead of "returns {valid:true} for any non-empty key". Add a test asserting empty-body POST returns 200 {valid:false}. Whether to gate/disable the endpoint until a real license store exists is a product decision to surface to the user, not part of the minimal fix.
confirmed.verify_reason: Dead EOF guard confirmed with exact evidence and an empirical check: services/r1-coord-api/main.go:177 uses `errors.Is(err, fmt.Errorf("EOF"))`, which I verified can never match (`errors.Is(io.EOF, fmt.Errorf("EOF"))` == false in a standalone Go run), so an empty-body POST /v1/license/verify returns 400 "invalid JSON body" instead of the intended 200 {valid:false} — intent proven by the correct `errors.Is(err, io.EOF)` in the sibling telemetry handler at main.go:196. Tests (main_test.go:30-53) cover only long/short key, never empty body, so the dead branch is untested. The second half of the claim is accurate but overstated: main.go:181 does accept any 8+ char key on a public path (main.go:447) with reason "well-formed key" (main.go:185), but the file header (main.go:7) explicitly documents the endpoint as a "license-key shape stub", and grep across cmd/, internal/, desktop/, web/ shows nothing in this repo consumes /v1/license/verify to gate functionality — so there is no enforcement to bypass and no security consequence today. Bonus defect: main.go:7 says "returns {valid:true} for any non-empty key" while the code requires >= 8 chars (doc/code mismatch in the same file). Net: real correctness bug plus misleading doc/reason strings; not a licensing security hole.

confirmed.title: Two enabled SevMajor convergence rules always return nil — advertised test-coverage gates never fire
confirmed.evidence: missingTestFileRule (ID "missing-test-file", Severity: SevMajor, Enabled: true) ends `return nil // Handled at integration level, not per-file` (line 670), and missingErrorTestRule (ID "no-missing-error-test", SevMajor, Enabled: true) ends `return nil // Handled at integration level (cross-file), not per-file` (line 1054). Grep for any integration-level handling of these rule IDs finds only these two comments — no cross-file promotion exists anywhere in internal/convergence. The adversarial self-audit therefore silently skips both checks while counting them among its enabled gates.
confirmed.fix: In internal/convergence/validator.go, add an integration-phase pass crossFileTestCoverageFindings(files []FileInput, enabled map[string]bool) []Finding, called from both Validate (after line 198 wg.Wait()) and ValidateWithCriteria (after line 244), gated on the rule IDs being enabled so EnableRule() still works. For "missing-test-file": for each non-test .go file in the input set, emit a SevMajor CatTestCoverage finding if no _test.go exists in the same directory within the set. For "no-missing-error-test": collect error-returning function names via the existing errorReturnFunc regex, concatenate all _test.go contents in the set, and emit one finding per source file whose error-returning functions never appear in test content alongside err/Error. Replace the misleading per-file stub bodies with comments pointing at the integration function (keep the Rule entries as the enable/disable registry so RulesApplied stays honest). Add validator tests: source-only file set fires both rules; source+covering tests fires neither. Alternative minimal fix if partial-file-set false positives are unacceptable: set Enabled:false on both rules with an honest comment and update the 74-rule pin at validator_test.go:843.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at HEAD: both rules' Check funcs unconditionally return nil (validator.go:670 and :1054) after trivial early-outs, yet both are Enabled:true SevMajor and registered in DefaultRules() (validator.go:404-405), so they are counted in Report.RulesApplied (validator.go:332, pinned at 74 by validator_test.go:843). The comments claim 'Handled at integration level' but repo-wide grep for the rule IDs hits only validator.go — no caller or integration layer exists. SemanticAnalysis's only CatTestCoverage check (semantic.go:565-575, RuleID 'criteria-semantic') is criteria-keyword matching, runs only when criteria are supplied (Validate passes nil), and does not check per-file test existence or error-path tests. Consequence: the adversarial self-audit advertises two test-coverage gates that can never fire — missions adding untested source files or untested error paths get no finding and no SevMajor score deduction, and missingErrorTestRule even runs its regex then discards all matches. Fixable in-repo since Validate/ValidateWithCriteria already hold the full []FileInput set.

confirmed.verify_reason: Verified both endpoints in the working tree. Server: internal/server/ws.go:328-361 handleClientFrame routes only $/pong, $/ping, session.subscribe, session.unsubscribe; default arm (line 360) returns -32601. Client: internal/tui/lanes/lanes_transport.go issues r1.lanes.list (674), r1.lanes.kill (975), r1.lanes.killAll (988), r1.lanes.pin (996) over the same WS, and its doc comment (404-408) admits the server does not route them. confirmed.title: License verification endpoint is shape-only (any 8+ char key is valid) and its doc comment contradicts the code
confirmed.evidence: `valid := len(req.Key) >= 8` — the deployed /v1/license/verify endpoint approves any 8+ character string; there is no key store, signature, or tenant lookup, and nothing in cmd/ or internal/ calls this endpoint, so licensing is enforced nowhere. The package doc (line 7) additionally claims "returns {valid:true} for any non-empty key", which the code contradicts (short keys are rejected — see main_test.go:44).
confirmed.fix: Two one-line changes in services/r1-coord-api/main.go: (1) line 7 — correct the package doc to match behavior: "POST /v1/license/verify — license-key shape stub; returns {valid:true} for any key of 8+ chars (no key registry; deliberate stub, see docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md)". (2) line 177 — replace `errors.Is(err, fmt.Errorf("EOF"))` with `errors.Is(err, io.EOF)` (the current expression is always false, so an empty POST body returns 400 "invalid JSON body" instead of the intended {valid:false} passthrough; matches the correct pattern already used at line 196). Drop the "back it with a real key registry" prong from the finding — docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md:224 explicitly defers that to "before the real auth integration lands" and no client in the repo calls the endpoint.
confirmed.verify_reason: Partially confirmed, severity downgraded. The code facts are accurate: services/r1-coord-api/main.go:181 has `valid := len(req.Key) >= 8`, and the package doc at main.go:7 ("returns {valid:true} for any non-empty key") contradicts both the code and the package's own test (main_test.go:44-53 asserts valid=false for non-empty key "x"). However, the severe framing ("licensing is enforced nowhere") is refuted as a finding: docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md:224 explicitly declares "License-verify and telemetry-opt-in stubs are deliberate — they answer 200 with well-formed JSON so the DNS chain can be smoke-tested before the real auth integration lands" — i.e., intentional, documented design, and a repo-wide grep confirms zero callers (only docs, the service, and its tests reference /v1/license/verify), so no client trusts the shape-only check and there is no user-visible enforcement hole today. What survives is the doc-comment-vs-code contradiction (a "docs claim things the code doesn't do" item) plus a corroborating real bug found during verification: main.go:177 uses `errors.Is(err, fmt.Errorf("EOF"))`, which is always false (fmt.Errorf mints a fresh error that matches nothing), so an empty POST body returns 400 instead of the intended EOF passthrough — the telemetry handler at main.go:196 does it correctly with `errors.Is(err, io.EOF)`. Both are trivially fixable in-repo.

confirmed.title: Documented 5-provider fallback chain can never fall past Codex/Native — OpenRouter/DirectAPI/Ember/LintOnly hardwired unavailable
confirmed.evidence: isAvailable in the workflow engine: `case model.ProviderOpenRouter, model.ProviderDirectAPI, model.ProviderEmber, model.ProviderLintOnly: return false // not yet wired as runners` (lines 1950-1953). CLAUDE.md key decision 15 and the package map advertise "model.Resolve() walks Primary -> FallbackChain (Claude -> Codex -> OpenRouter -> API -> lint-only)" and "5-provider fallback", but the executing layer permanently reports those providers unavailable, so the fallback chain is 2-3 providers in practice and the lint-only last resort never engages.
confirmed.fix: Immediate (docs correction, one commit): (1) CLAUDE.md decision 15 + model/ package-map line: state the automatic fallback currently resolves Claude → Codex (Native via --runner-mode/modelsource); OpenRouter/DirectAPI/Ember/lint-only are defined in internal/model/router.go but not wired as workflow runners (engine.APIRunner exists, unused in production). (2) docs/README.md:151 and docs/FEATURE-MAP.md:12: change Status from Done to In Progress/Scoped for the OpenRouter/direct-API/lint-only tiers. (3) docs/BUSINESS-VALUE.md:123 and :194: remove or rewrite the "lint-only mode keeps the missions on the rails" and "isn't theoretical" claims. (4) app.go:541-557: relabel doctor's OpenRouter/Direct API/Lint-only entries as "configured (router-defined, not yet wired as execution runner)" so the diagnostic stops implying automatic engagement. Optional follow-up feature (separate spec, not required to close the drift): add an APIRunner field to engine.Registry, construct it in buildRunners when OPENROUTER_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present, map ProviderOpenRouter/ProviderDirectAPI in providerToRunner and flip isAvailable; add a lint-only runner that skips model execution and runs only the verify pipeline for ProviderLintOnly.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at HEAD: workflow.go:1950-1953 hardwires OpenRouter/DirectAPI/Ember/LintOnly to unavailable ("not yet wired as runners"); engine.Registry (types.go:367-372) has only Claude/Codex/Native slots; the OpenRouter-capable engine.APIRunner has zero production callers; and providerToRunner (workflow.go:1987-1988) maps even a LintOnly resolution back to the Claude runner, so no lint-only execution mode exists. Worse, buildRunners (app.go:464-488) always constructs a non-nil Claude runner, so isAvailable(Claude) is always true and the chain never advances past hop 1 — a missing binary yields exec errors, not degradation. Docs claim the opposite: docs/README.md:151 and docs/FEATURE-MAP.md:12 mark the five-provider fallback "Done", docs/BUSINESS-VALUE.md:123/194 say "lint-only mode keeps the missions on the rails" and "isn't theoretical", and r1 doctor --providers (app.go:541-557) prints OpenRouter/DirectAPI/Lint-only as an active "Provider fallback chain". Concrete consequence: an operator with OPENROUTER_API_KEY configured (doctor shows [ok]) expects automatic degradation when Claude/Codex rate-limit; instead missions fail outright. Softening nuance: OpenRouter/direct-API execution is reachable via the SOW fast path's modelsource (cmd/r1/main.go:2765-2797, BUILDER_SOURCE=openrouter), but that is explicit operator routing of the Native runner, not the advertised automatic fallback — the finding stands as scoped. This is docs-drift (docs claiming behavior code doesn't do), not a runtime correctness bug, hence P2.

confirmed.title: Documented env vars STOKE_RETENTION and STOKE_MASTER_KEY_FILE are read by no code
confirmed.evidence: env-vars.mdx:122 documents `STOKE_RETENTION` as "`1` enables the default retention profile when no operator config exists", but grep across cmd/, internal/, services/ finds no os.Getenv/LookupEnv for it — the only hit is a comment at internal/retention/policy.go:75. docs/operations/session-migration.md:148 tells operators to "Provision via STOKE_MASTER_KEY_FILE" for key_material_mismatch recovery, but no Go code reads STOKE_MASTER_KEY_FILE anywhere. Both are operator instructions that provably do nothing.
confirmed.fix: Two-part fix. (1) STOKE_RETENTION: implement the spec's gate rather than deleting the doc row, because the current unconditional sweep violates the spec's opt-in retain-forever promise and deletes operator data by default — in cmd/r1-server/main.go:181 wrap startRetentionSweep in `if os.Getenv("STOKE_RETENTION") == "1"` (spec item 33), and keep env-vars.mdx:122 as-is; optionally log one DEBUG line when unset per spec §242. Additionally (same commit or follow-up) make cmd/r1/retention_policy.go actually store the policy (package-level var + getRetentionPolicy) or delete the misleading 'stored for downstream consumption' comment at cmd/r1/main.go:1832-1836. (2) STOKE_MASTER_KEY_FILE: fix docs/operations/session-migration.md:148 to describe the real provisioning path — copy the source machine's FileKeyring entry `~/.r1/keyring/<base64url("master-key")>.key` to the destination's keyring dir (or use the OS keyring backend per R1_KEYRING_BACKEND) — and remove the STOKE_MASTER_KEY_FILE mention, or alternatively implement it in internal/encryption/master_key.go resolveDefaultMasterKeyring (read 32-byte key from the file path in STOKE_MASTER_KEY_FILE before falling back to the keyring) and update specs/cross-machine-session-migration.md:234 accordingly. The doc-only variant is the lower-risk fix.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified: no Getenv/LookupEnv for STOKE_RETENTION or STOKE_MASTER_KEY_FILE anywhere in cmd/, internal/, services/, desktop/, web/ (only comment at internal/retention/policy.go:75 and spec mentions). The claim actually understates the problem. (1) STOKE_RETENTION: env-vars.mdx:122 says '1 enables the default retention profile', but the profile runs unconditionally — cmd/r1-server/main.go:181 starts the hourly sweep with retention.Defaults() and no gate, and EnforceSweep genuinely deletes data (os.Remove at internal/retention/enforce.go:339: stream files >90d, checkpoints >30d). specs/retention-policies.md:242 promises retain-forever when the var is unset (gating items 32/33 unchecked), so operators relying on the documented opt-in gate silently lose data. Also found while verifying: cmd/r1/retention_policy.go:47-49 setRetentionPolicy discards its policy (`_ = p.Validate()`) despite main.go:1832 claiming it is stored for enforcement hooks, and EnforceOnSessionEnd has zero callers — so --retention-permanent does not affect the r1-server sweep either. (2) STOKE_MASTER_KEY_FILE: session-migration.md:148 offers two remediations and both are fake — the env var is read nowhere, and ~/.r1/master.key is also read nowhere; the real location is ~/.r1/keyring/<base64url("master-key")>.key via FileKeyring (internal/encryption/master_key.go:85-91, keyring.go:151,175). An operator recovering from key_material_mismatch per the doc will fail. Concrete user-visible consequences on both counts; fixes are entirely in-repo.

confirmed.title: All downloadable r1 binaries ship with stub SQLite (CGO_ENABLED=0) and without the sqlite_fts5 tag — --sqlite store, research/wisdom/membus FTS, migration idempotency all inert in shipped binaries
confirmed.evidence: cloudbuild.yaml:133-136 builds the published binaries with `CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=$$OS ... go build -mod=vendor -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=$SHORT_SHA"` (no -tags sqlite_fts5); cloudbuild-binaries.yaml:36-38 same (CGO_ENABLED=0, `-ldflags "-s -w"`). The only SQLite driver is cgo-only mattn/go-sqlite3 (go.mod:31 + replace at :74); vendor/github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/static_mock.go:16 makes every Open fail at runtime: "Binary was compiled with 'CGO_ENABLED=0', go-sqlite3 requires cgo to work. This is a stub". This contradicts remediation-triage F1 "STATUS: FIXED" and internal/research/fts5_active_test.go:8's claim that "the shipped binary is built with -tags sqlite_fts5" — F1 only fixed Makefile:16 and install.sh:56, not the binary-release channels. Every advertised SQLite feature (cmd/r1/main.go:7161 `--sqlite`, session.db auto-detect at main.go:4120, research FTS5, wisdom/sqlite, membus, migration_imports) errors at runtime in the binaries users download.
confirmed.fix: (1) cloudbuild.yaml build-multi-platform-r1 step and cloudbuild-binaries.yaml: for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, apt-get install gcc-x86-64-linux-gnu gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu (as cloudbuild-release.yaml:16-17 already does) and build with CGO_ENABLED=1, CC set per arch, adding -tags sqlite_fts5. (2) For darwin/windows cross-builds in those pipelines, keep CGO_ENABLED=0 (osxcross is not available) but add a `//go:build !cgo` guard file in cmd/r1 (or a doctor check that Pings sqlite3 :memory:) so --sqlite/session.db auto-detect fail fast with "this build has no SQLite support; install via install.sh or brew" instead of the raw stub error, and document the degradation in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md. (3) Add -tags sqlite_fts5 to .goreleaser.yml r1 build flags (line 17-18) and to the Dockerfile go build (line 13) so tagged releases and the container image get FTS5. (4) Correct the comment in internal/research/fts5_active_test.go:7-9 to name the channels that actually guarantee the tag, and append a correction note to audit/remediation-triage-2026-06-02.md F1 (do not silently rewrite the FIXED entry).
confirmed.verify_reason: CONFIRMED with one scope correction. Verified in the working tree: (1) cloudbuild.yaml:133-138 and cloudbuild-binaries.yaml:36-40 build all published binaries with CGO_ENABLED=0 and no -tags sqlite_fts5, publishing to gs://relayone-488319-public/r1/{SHA,latest} (cloudbuild.yaml:149-152,159). (2) This bucket IS the user-facing download channel: services/r1-downloads-cdn/main.go:169-182 redirects every asset >30 MiB (r1 is ~64 MiB per the comment at :170-171) to https://storage.googleapis.com/relayone-488319-public/r1/latest/ — so real web downloads get the CGO=0 binaries. (3) The only SQLite driver is cgo-only: go.mod:31 mattn/go-sqlite3, replace at go.mod:74 to the jgiannuzzi cgo fork; vendor/github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/static_mock.go:16 makes every Open error with the "requires cgo" stub message; no pure-Go driver exists. (4) Concrete user-visible failure: internal/session/sqlstore.go:53-61 NewSQLStore runs migrate() immediately, so in these binaries `r1 status` fatals at cmd/r1/main.go:4123 ("sqlite store: ...") whenever --sqlite is passed OR .stoke/session.db merely exists (auto-detect at main.go:4120-4122); research/wisdom/membus SQLite stores fail the same way. (5) F1 in audit/remediation-triage-2026-06-02.md:32-44 claims "STATUS: FIXED (commit: 72053d5f)" for "FTS5 compiled out of every shipped binary", but git show 72053d5f confirms it touched only Makefile, install.sh, and the memory-bridge files — no release pipeline; repo-wide grep confirms Makefile:16 and install.sh:56 are the ONLY build paths with -tags sqlite_fts5. So: GCS/CDN channel = stub SQLite (hard runtime errors); goreleaser/GitHub channel = working SQLite, dormant FTS5. Both contradict the F1 FIXED claim and the test comment. confirmed.title: README's documented install path downloads.r1.run/prod/r1-linux-amd64 is structurally a 404: no pipeline in the repo ever publishes objects under the CDN's prod/staging/dev channels
confirmed.evidence: README.md:90 instructs `curl -fsSL https://downloads.r1.run/prod/r1-$(uname ...)`. services/r1-downloads-cdn/main.go:50 serves bucket relayone-488319-r1-releases and :140 rejects anything but channels prod/staging/dev; :151-156 404s when obj.Attrs fails. But the only publisher to that bucket is cloudbuild-release.yaml:46, which uploads `dist/*.tar.gz checksums.txt` to `gs://relayone-488319-r1-releases/<TAG>/` — tarballs under a tag prefix, never a `prod/r1-linux-amd64` raw binary. The per-push raw binaries go to a different bucket entirely (cloudbuild.yaml:150 `gs://relayone-488319-public/r1/<sha|latest>/`). The 2026-06-12 finish-gap audit probed this path as HTTP 404; the only change since (commit 223b356f, >30MiB redirect at main.go:176) still requires the private-bucket object to exist first, so the path remains dead by construction.
confirmed.fix: Two-part fix, both in-repo. (1) Pipeline: add a channel-publish step to cloudbuild-binaries.yaml (after publish-r1-binaries) or cloudbuild.yaml (after line 151) that also copies dist/r1-* to gs://relayone-488319-r1-releases/prod/ on main/tag builds (and staging/dev per branch if those triggers exist), e.g. `for f in dist/*; do gcloud storage cp "$$f" gs://relayone-488319-r1-releases/prod/$$(basename "$$f"); done`. Note: the Cloud Build SA may need storage.objectAdmin on that bucket — if the grant is missing, list that single IAM grant as a P3 ci-gap/operator item, but the config change itself is in-repo. (2) Docs: until/unless (1) is verified live, repoint the install command at the layout that is actually populated on every push — https://storage.googleapis.com/relayone-488319-public/r1/latest/r1-$(uname -s | tr A-Z a-z)-$(uname -m | sed s/x86_64/amd64/) — in README.md:90, docs/README.md:90, docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:76, docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md:27; and in all cases correct the false statement at docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:221 ('Per-channel binaries land here via cloudbuild-binaries.yaml on tag push') to describe the real publisher/layout.
confirmed.verify_reason: Confirmed with direct evidence at HEAD e88f48a7. README.md:90 (and docs/README.md:90, docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:76, docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md:27) document GET https://downloads.r1.run/prod/r1-<os>-<arch> as the primary install path. services/r1-downloads-cdn/main.go:50 serves bucket relayone-488319-r1-releases, main.go:138-143 accepts only prod/staging/dev channels, and main.go:151-156 404s when obj.Attrs fails; the >30MiB redirect at main.go:176-182 is unreachable unless the private-bucket object prod/r1-linux-amd64 already exists, so it cannot rescue the path (and git log confirms 223b356f is the only CDN/pipeline commit since the 2026-06-12 audit that live-probed this URL as HTTP 404). Exhaustive search of all publishers: the only writer to relayone-488319-r1-releases is cloudbuild-release.yaml:46-47, which uploads dist/*.tar.gz + checksums.txt under gs://…/$TAG_NAME/ — a tag prefix the CDN rejects as an invalid channel, and tarballs, not the raw asset name. Raw binaries go to a different bucket (cloudbuild.yaml:150-151 and cloudbuild-binaries.yaml:2,56-59 → gs://relayone-488319-public/r1/{sha|build-id,latest}/). No workflow, script, install.sh, or deploy.sh writes channel objects (deploy.sh:150 only grants read IAM). Not intentional design: no manual-promote runbook exists, and docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:221 falsely claims 'Per-channel binaries land here via cloudbuild-binaries.yaml on tag push' — that file writes the public bucket, never channel prefixes. User-visible consequence: every user following the first Quick Start command gets a guaranteed 404; curl produces no file and chmod fails. confirmed.title: Tag-release pipeline cannot succeed: .goreleaser.yml darwin builds require o64-clang (osxcross) which cloudbuild-release.yaml never installs
confirmed.evidence: cloudbuild-release.yaml:16-17 installs only `gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu gcc-x86-64-linux-gnu gcc`, then runs `goreleaser release` with CGO_ENABLED=1. .goreleaser.yml:15-16 sets CGO_ENABLED=1 for the r1 build and its darwin overrides (:35-41) set `CC=o64-clang` — a toolchain that does not exist in the golang:1.25 image, so the darwin/amd64 and darwin/arm64 legs fail and goreleaser aborts the whole release. The v-tag release channel (which feeds the relayone-488319-r1-releases bucket the downloads CDN reads) is therefore broken as configured.
confirmed.fix: Two changes, both in-repo: (1) .goreleaser.yml — remove darwin from the CGO_ENABLED=1 'r1' build (keep linux amd64/arm64 with the existing gcc overrides) and add a separate 'r1-darwin' build id with binary 'r1', CGO_ENABLED=0, goos [darwin], goarch [amd64, arm64], mirroring the r1-acp pattern at .goreleaser.yml:44-61; mattn/go-sqlite3 compiles under !cgo with a runtime-error stub, and cloudbuild-binaries.yaml already ships CGO_ENABLED=0 darwin r1 binaries, so this matches existing distribution behavior (osxcross install is the alternative but requires a macOS SDK and is not justified). (2) cloudbuild-release.yaml — install goreleaser inside the 'goreleaser' step itself (or collapse install-deps into it), because /usr/local/bin does not persist across Cloud Build step containers and line 32 currently fails with 'goreleaser: command not found'. Optional while touching it: check whether research/ FTS5 needs -tags sqlite_fts5 under the sqlite3mc replace; only add the tag if go test ./internal/research/... fails without it (CI currently passes without it, suggesting the fork enables FTS5 by default).
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at cloudbuild-release.yaml:16-17,30-31 — only linux gcc cross-compilers installed — while .goreleaser.yml:36-43 sets CC=o64-clang for both darwin legs of the CGO_ENABLED=1 'r1' build. The cgo need is real (go.mod:31 mattn/go-sqlite3, replaced at go.mod:74 with the sqlite3mc fork), so the darwin legs fail with 'exec: o64-clang: not found' and goreleaser aborts; upload-gcs and docker-build-push both waitFor the goreleaser step, so ${TAG}/ archives, checksums, SBOMs, and r1-agent:${TAG}/:latest Docker images are never produced. No fallback exists: .github/workflows/ contains no release workflow. Verification also found a second independent fatal defect: goreleaser is installed to /usr/local/bin only in the install-deps step container (lines 19-20), and Cloud Build steps share only /workspace, so the goreleaser step (line 32) fails with 'command not found' before the darwin legs are even reached — the pipeline as written has never been runnable. One overstatement in the original claim: the r1-downloads-cdn only lists prod|staging|dev channel prefixes (services/r1-downloads-cdn/main.go:16,110-114) fed by cloudbuild-binaries.yaml per DEPLOYMENT.md:222, and this pipeline uploads to gs://bucket/${TAG}/, so the CDN channels are not the affected consumer — the tag-archive and Docker-image channels are. Severity P2 rather than P1/P0: release automation only, a parallel CGO_ENABLED=0 binaries pipeline (cloudbuild-binaries.yaml) still ships user-facing binaries, and trigger wiring is operator-side.

confirmed.title: r1-browser deploy smoke step can never pass: unauthenticated external curl against a service deployed with --no-allow-unauthenticated AND internal-only ingress
confirmed.evidence: cloudbuild-r1-browser.yaml:58 deploys with `--no-allow-unauthenticated` and :69 `--ingress=internal-and-cloud-load-balancing`, then the smoke step (:80-95) does a plain `curl ... "$$URL/livez"` from the Cloud Build worker expecting 200 ("/livez is unauthenticated (it's outside the WS path)" — true only at app level). The request is rejected at both the ingress layer (external caller) and the IAM layer (no identity token), so smoke always exits 1 and the deploy pipeline is red by construction. This is the still-open residue of the finish-gap item 'deploy r1-browser service or strike C6 from live claims' — the service dir + config exist but the deploy config is incoherent.
confirmed.fix: In services/cloudbuild-r1-browser.yaml, replace the post-deploy external curl smoke with (a) a hermetic pre-deploy container smoke after the build step: docker run -d -p 8080:8080 -e R1_BROWSER_SKIP_CHROMIUM=1 us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT_ID/r1/r1-browser:$SHORT_SHA, then curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' localhost:8080/livez expecting 200 (the R1_BROWSER_SKIP_CHROMIUM override at services/r1-browser/main.go:75-79 serves /livez without Chromium), and (b) a post-deploy control-plane readiness check that works despite internal ingress: gcloud run services describe r1-browser-${_ENV} --region=${_REGION} --format='value(status.conditions)' asserting Ready=True (authenticated gcloud API call, not data-plane HTTP). Also fix the misleading comment at :84 and update docs/operations/r1-browser-service.md §4 step 3 to include -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-identity-token)" and to note the caller must be inside the VPC (Cloud Shell is not). Do NOT relax ingress or auth — the locked-down posture is deliberate per the ops doc §2.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at services/cloudbuild-r1-browser.yaml: line 58 deploys with --no-allow-unauthenticated, line 69 with --ingress=internal-and-cloud-load-balancing, and the smoke step (lines 80-95) plain-curls the run.app /livez URL from the Cloud Build worker expecting 200. No private worker pool is configured, so the worker is outside the VPC: the request is rejected at the ingress layer (404) before IAM, and would be 403 at IAM regardless — the loop can never see 200, so the step deterministically exits 1 after a successful deploy. Not intentional design: the comment at :84 conflates app-level auth (/livez is open in main.go:60,89-93) with platform layers; the sibling cloudbuild-deploy.yaml uses the same curl pattern but with --allow-unauthenticated (lines 123/161/197/238), showing the pattern was copied without adapting to the locked-down posture; and docs/operations/r1-browser-service.md §4 (lines 81-85) instructs operators to run exactly this config, then separately prescribes manual smoke 'from a Cloud Shell or VM in the VPC' (line 87), contradicting the pipeline's built-in external curl. Consequence: the documented first staging/prod deploy of r1-browser (the still-open finish-gap item, audit/r1-finish-gap-2026-06-12.md:38,122) reports red on every run despite the deploy step succeeding. One correction to the finder's fix: an identity token alone does NOT fix it (ingress still 404s the external worker), and relaxing ingress to 'all' would undo the documented security posture (ops doc line 35).

confirmed.title: Conflict-auto-resolution merge path has zero coverage anywhere (Merge/detectConflicts/applyConflictResolutions all 0.0%)
confirmed.evidence: `go tool cover -func` on internal/worktree: manager.go:246 Merge 0.0%, manager.go:318 allAutoResolved 0.0%, manager.go:337 applyConflictResolutions 0.0%, conflicts.go:114 detectConflicts 0.0%, helpers.go:430 ValidateMerge 0.0%, helpers.go:489 ResetMainTo 0.0%. Root integration_test.go exercises only the happy path — its own section header at line 184 reads "Parallel worktrees (non-conflicting merges)" and no test in the repo greps for a forced conflict through Merge. This is the code that AUTO-RESOLVES git conflicts and commits the result to main (design decisions #8/#9); package coverage is 49.0%.
confirmed.fix: Two-part fix in internal/worktree: (1) Repair the dead wiring in Manager.Merge (manager.go:255-310): merge-tree --write-tree output never contains conflict markers, so stop Parse-ing it. Instead, on real-merge failure, list conflicted files via `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`, read each working-tree file (which DOES contain <<<<<<< markers), call conflictres.Parse(content, file) per file (fixing the empty-File bug at manager.go:265), AutoResolve, then reuse applyConflictResolutions to Resolve/stage/commit, keeping the existing merge --abort fallback when any conflict is not auto-resolved. (2) Add integration tests that build a temp git repo with a forced two-branch content conflict and drive Manager.Merge end-to-end: assert (a) an auto-resolvable conflict (e.g., competing import lines per conflictres classify rules) merges and commits resolved content to main, (b) an unresolvable semantic conflict returns an error, aborts the merge (no MERGE_HEAD, clean status), and leaves main untouched, and (c) add a test exercising detectConflicts via the ConflictScanner path (conflicts.go:56) with two overlapping worktrees.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified by running coverage myself: per-package numbers match exactly, and cross-package coverage (-coverpkg over root, workflow, app, orchestrate, cmd/r1 tests) confirms allAutoResolved (manager.go:318), applyConflictResolutions (manager.go:337), detectConflicts (conflicts.go:114), and ResetMainTo (helpers.go:489) are 0.0% everywhere; Merge is only 37.8% (happy path via root integration_test.go, which the finder acknowledged). No test in the repo forces a conflict through Manager.Merge. Two corrections: ValidateMerge (helpers.go:430) is actually 83.3% covered via internal/workflow tests, and the finding is understated — I empirically probed `git merge-tree --write-tree` on a real content conflict and its output contains NO `<<<<<<<` markers (only tree OID, stage entries, and CONFLICT messages), while conflictres.Parse (resolver.go:51) detects conflicts solely by scanning for `<<<<<<<`. Therefore Parse(mergeOutput, "") at manager.go:265 always returns zero conflicts, Merge always falls to the hard-fail at line 283, and the entire auto-resolution branch (manager.go:266-281, 297-306, 318-395) is unreachable dead code — additionally, Parse is called with file="" so Conflict.File would be empty and applyConflictResolutions would os.ReadFile the repo root and fail even if markers appeared. Concrete user-visible consequence: parallel-task merges with auto-resolvable conflicts (imports/whitespace/duplicates) always hard-fail despite the advertised semantic auto-resolution feature, and the code path that rewrites files and commits to main carries zero test evidence. The missing conflict-forcing test is exactly what would have caught this dormancy; fully fixable in-repo.

confirmed.title: Claude/Codex CLI runners: ctx cancellation SIGKILLs only the process-group leader, orphaning child processes

The group kill (`killProcessGroup`, claude.go:191 / codex.go:183) runs solely on the post-result-timeout path. So cancelling the run ctx (scheduler cancel, boulder execCancel at workflow.go:469, Ctrl-C) leaves node/bash/MCP children in the new pgid running as orphans, still writing into the worktree. confirmed.fix: In internal/engine/claude.go (after line 137) and internal/engine/codex.go (after line 76), immediately after procutil.ConfigureProcessGroup(cmd), set: cmd.Cancel = func() error { return procutil.Terminate(cmd) } and cmd.WaitDelay = 5 * time.Second, then in the waitDone branch call killProcessGroup(cmd) when ctx.Err() != nil to guarantee SIGTERM→SIGKILL group escalation (or, simpler and consistent with tools.go:966-978 / hub/transport.go:60-64, use cmd.Cancel = func() error { return procutil.Kill(cmd) } + WaitDelay). confirmed.title: Boulder idle-nudge fires -> guaranteed deadlock: Scan holds mutex while nudge callback re-enters RecordActivity
confirmed.evidence: Scan() takes `e.mu.Lock(); defer e.mu.Unlock()` (enforcer.go:162-163) and invokes the caller's callback while holding the lock: `delivered := nudge(task.ID, msg)` (line 209). The only production wiring, internal/workflow/workflow.go:456-486, passes a NudgeFunc that calls `e.OnEvent(...)` (workflow.go:460-465) — and OnEvent was wrapped at workflow.go:481-486 to call `e.Boulder.RecordActivity()` first, which takes the same non-reentrant `e.mu` (enforcer.go:153-157). Scan -> nudge -> OnEvent -> RecordActivity -> e.mu.Lock() self-deadlocks.
confirmed.fix: Primary fix in internal/boulder/enforcer.go Scan(): perform the throttle/pause/idle checks and snapshot the nudge candidates (task ID, message, current nudgeCount, backoff eligibility) under e.mu, then release the lock before invoking the nudge callback for each candidate, then re-acquire e.mu to append NudgeRecords, update ConsecFailures/PausedUntil, and saveState. Document on NudgeFunc that it is invoked without the enforcer lock and may safely call back into the Enforcer. Secondary hardening in internal/workflow/workflow.go: move the OnEvent wrap (lines 479-486) to before the scanner goroutine is started to remove the unsynchronized write/read race on e.OnEvent, and optionally have the nudge closure emit via origOnEvent so a nudge does not reset the idle timer it just detected. Add a regression test that calls Scan with a NudgeFunc that invokes RecordActivity (guarded by a timeout) to prove no deadlock.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified in current tree: internal/boulder/enforcer.go:162-163 holds e.mu for the whole Scan body via defer, and line 209 calls the nudge callback under that lock; RecordActivity (enforcer.go:153-157) takes the same non-reentrant sync.Mutex. The only production wiring, internal/workflow/workflow.go:456-486, passes a NudgeFunc that calls e.OnEvent, which lines 479-486 rewrap to call e.Boulder.RecordActivity() first (and the wrapper is always non-nil after line 481). So the first delivered nudge self-deadlocks: Scan -> nudge -> wrapped OnEvent -> RecordActivity -> e.mu.Lock(). The MaxNudges/execCancel escalation (workflow.go:467-470) is unreachable because the closure never returns. Blast radius: the deadlocked scanner holds e.mu forever, so the wrapped OnEvent passed to the engine (workflow.go:497) blocks on every subsequent agent event, UpdateStatus at workflow.go:1240 blocks at completion, and since the build path shares one enforcer across all parallel tasks (cmd/r1/main.go:306-307) every task's event pipeline freezes. Boulder is always enabled on the run path (main.go:1145 'Always enabled'). Trigger is the feature's normal case: 30s without stream events (DefaultConfig IdleTimeout, enforcer.go:72) with an incomplete tracked task, e.g. a long silent tool call. Tests (enforcer_test.go:48-159) only use trivial non-reentrant closures, so they never catch it. No refutation applies: no re-entrancy handling, no documented restriction on NudgeFunc, scenario occurs in routine operation, fix is local Go code.

confirmed.title: Scheduler.Run deadlocks on context cancellation: wg.Wait() with no receiver draining results
confirmed.evidence: Worker goroutines (lines 219-230) send to `results` but never call wg.Done(); wg.Done() only happens on the receive paths (drainResults line 177, blocking select line 272). The cancellation branch is `case <-ctx.Done(): wg.Wait(); return allResults, ctx.Err()` (lines 276-278) — after ctx cancels we stop receiving, so the WaitGroup counter for every in-flight task never reaches zero and wg.Wait() blocks forever. Concrete: Ctrl-C / run-timeout with >=1 task executing (cmd/r1/main.go:554 `sched.Run(ctx, p, execFn)`) hangs the whole r1 process instead of returning ctx.Err().
confirmed.fix: In the ctx.Done() branch of Scheduler.Run (internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:276-278), drain in-flight results before returning instead of bare wg.Wait(): `case <-ctx.Done(): for active > 0 { r := <-results; wg.Done(); active--; allResults = append(allResults, r); recordResult(r) }; wg.Wait(); return allResults, ctx.Err()`. This is bounded because execFn honors ctx (engine runners kill process groups on cancel) and preserves in-flight results/bookkeeping. Prefer this over the finder's alternative of moving `defer wg.Done()` into the worker goroutine, which would return without appending in-flight results to allResults or running recordResult (dropping file-lock release and bus/dispatch events). Add a regression test: cancel ctx while one task is in flight, assert Run returns ctx.Err() within a watchdog timeout (the exact reproducer used for verification works as-is).
confirmed.verify_reason: Empirically reproduced deadlock. internal/scheduler/scheduler.go: wg.Add(1) at line 218 per dispatched task, but the worker goroutine (219-230) never calls wg.Done — the only wg.Done sites are the receive paths (line 176 drainResults, line 272 blocking select). The cancellation branch (276-278) does `case <-ctx.Done(): wg.Wait(); return` with no further receives, so the counter for every in-flight task never reaches zero and wg.Wait blocks forever (channel buffering is irrelevant; wg tracks receives, not sends). The scenario is reachable: cmd/r1/main.go:254-261 passes a signalContext (SIGINT/SIGTERM, main.go:628-648) optionally wrapped in WithTimeout(cfg.Timeout) into sched.Run at main.go:554 (TUI path main.go:1504 identical). Proven with a temporary in-package test cancelling ctx while one task was in flight: Run never returned (FAIL after 5s watchdog); reproducer deleted, tree clean. No existing scheduler test uses a cancellable context. User-visible: one Ctrl-C hangs r1 (second Ctrl-C hard-exits via os.Exit(1) at main.go:642, skipping session save/report/worktree cleanup); the run-timeout path in unattended/cron use hangs the process indefinitely.

confirmed.title: bus.restoreDelayed mutates b.delayed without the mutex while its own timers fire concurrently; past-due events can be lost
confirmed.evidence: restoreDelayed (called from New) arms `time.AfterFunc(remaining, ...)` with remaining clamped to 1ms for past-due entries (lines 868-871, 876) BEFORE inserting into the map with no lock held: `b.delayed[cancelID] = e` (line 887). The timer callback locks b.mu and reads/deletes the same map (878-885). With 2+ past-due entries, entry A's 1ms timer can run while the loop is still writing entry B → unsynchronized map write vs locked map access = data race / 'concurrent map writes' panic. Worse, if A's callback runs before line 887 executes, `b.delayed[cancelID]` lookup fails, the callback returns, then the insert lands — the delayed event never publishes and the entry leaks forever. Contrast PublishDelayed (794-828) which holds b.mu across the same sequence.
confirmed.fix: In restoreDelayed (internal/bus/bus.go:856-890), acquire b.mu for the restore loop and insert each entry into b.delayed under the lock, matching PublishDelayed's invariant. Since restoreDelayed runs before New returns and the callback's first action is b.mu.Lock(), holding the lock across the whole loop is safe (callbacks simply block until restore completes, then find their entry): after `entries, err := b.wal.ReadDelayed()`, add `b.mu.Lock(); defer b.mu.Unlock()`, keep the per-entry body unchanged (arm timer, then `b.delayed[cancelID] = e` — ordering no longer matters under the lock). Also delete the dead `_ = now // suppress lint` line 875 and the now-unused `now := time.Now()` at 862. Add a regression test: append 3+ past-due schedule records via wal.AppendDelayed, reopen the bus with -race, and assert all events publish exactly once (guards both the race and the lost-event window).
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at internal/bus/bus.go:856-890. restoreDelayed holds no lock: it arms time.AfterFunc (line 876, remaining clamped to 1ms for past-due entries at 868-871) BEFORE the unlocked map write `b.delayed[cancelID] = e` at line 887, while the timer callback (877-885) concurrently locks b.mu and reads/deletes the same map. The loop's unlocked writes have no happens-before edge with the callback's locked reads — a genuine Go data race that the runtime can escalate to an unrecoverable 'fatal error: concurrent map read and map write' during Bus startup. The lost-event scenario is also real: if a 1ms callback runs before line 887's insert, the lookup at 878 misses, the callback returns without publishing, the insert then lands, and the timer never re-fires — the delayed event is silently dropped for the process lifetime and the stale entry leaks in b.delayed until Close. PublishDelayed (794-828) holds b.mu across both timer arming and map insert, confirming restoreDelayed deviates from the intended invariant. Refutations tried and failed: (1) 'New hasn't returned' doesn't help — AfterFunc callbacks run concurrently regardless of pointer escape; (2) TestDelayedEventSurvivesRestart (bus_test.go:534) restores one entry with ~200ms remaining so the race window is never exercised; (3) reachability — PublishDelayed has zero production callers outside internal/bus (repo-wide grep), so exposure today is tests-only, which caps severity at P2, but the bus is the advertised v2 substrate and the bug triggers the moment delayed events are wired. Real correctness bug, fixable in-repo.

confirmed.title: Late lobe Notes are silently lost, contradicting the documented 'land on a future round' contract
confirmed.evidence: Publish stamps `n.Round = w.currentRound` at publish time (workspace.go:198); Drain returns only `n.Round >= sinceRound` (workspace.go:287) and MidturnNote further filters to exactly the new roundID (cortex.go:584-589). A slow lobe that finishes after MidturnNote's Drain(N) but before the next round's SetRound(N+1) publishes a Note stamped Round=N; the next drain asks for Round >= N+1, so the Note is never surfaced to the model — yet cortex.go:570-571 documents 'late Notes will surface on a future round's Drain'. Failure: lobe exceeds the 2s RoundDeadline (Wait error is logged and drain proceeds, cortex.go:568-577), publishes a SevWarning note 3s later during the main model call → note permanently invisible (only SevCritical still gates via UnresolvedCritical). drainedUpTo (workspace.go:291-294) is maintained but never used to filter, so it cannot catch these.
confirmed.fix: Switch Drain to an undrained-index cursor, and fix BOTH filter sites: (1) In internal/cortex/workspace.go, repurpose drainedUpTo as a note-index cursor: Drain returns w.notes[drainedUpTo:] (deep copy), then sets drainedUpTo = uint64(len(w.notes)); keep the (notes, cursor) signature with the cursor now meaning notes-consumed count. This also reconciles persist.go:142, which already sets drainedUpTo = len(w.notes) per spec cortex-core.md:712, so post-replay Drain correctly returns nothing. (2) In internal/cortex/cortex.go MidturnNote, remove the exact-round filter at lines 584-589 (otherwise late notes returned by the fixed Drain are still discarded) and render all drained notes under the current round header; optionally suffix late entries with their original Round for display. (3) Add the spec-mandated regression test (cortex-core.md:773): a lobe that publishes after Round.Wait times out must have its note appear in the NEXT MidturnNote block; also update TestDrainAdvancesCursor for index semantics. Keep the sinceRound parameter in the signature (ignored or asserted) or drop it and update the two call sites — either is contained to internal/cortex.
confirmed.verify_reason: CONFIRMED. Publish stamps n.Round = w.currentRound at publish time (internal/cortex/workspace.go:198); currentRound only advances when the NEXT MidturnNote calls SetRound (cortex.go:554). Drain filters purely by n.Round >= sinceRound (workspace.go:286-288); drainedUpTo (workspace.go:291-294) is advanced but never used as a filter, and cortex.go:579 is its only production caller. Slow lobes are not cancelled — lobe.Run gets the runner lifetime context (lobe.go:290) and MidturnNote proceeds past Wait timeout (cortex.go:568-577) — so a lobe finishing after Drain(N) but before the next round's SetRound(N+1) (i.e., during the entire main-model inference span, the longest window in the turn) publishes a note stamped Round=N that Drain(N+1) excludes forever; the exact-round filter at cortex.go:584-589 would exclude it a second time. This directly contradicts cortex.go:570-571 and specs/cortex-core.md:773 gotcha #6, which states late notes "carry a later Round value" and mandates "Tests must assert that a slow Lobe does NOT lose its Note (it just lands on the next round's Drain)" — no such test exists (verified in cortex_test.go, round_test.go, cortex_integration_test.go). No rescue path: PreEndTurnGate covers only SevCritical (cortex.go:633); the hub event reaches UI subscribers, not the model. With the 2s default RoundDeadline, LLM-backed lobes (e.g. cortex/lobes/antitrunc emitting SevWarning on scope underdelivery) will routinely publish in this window, so warning/advice notes are silently dropped in the common case, not an edge race. Corroborating defect: persist.go:142 sets drainedUpTo = len(w.notes) (index semantics, matching spec cortex-core.md:712) while Drain sets it to sinceRound+1 (round-id semantics) — the same field holds two different units, confirming the cursor design is broken.

confirmed.title: Cortex BudgetTracker 30% lobe-output cap is collected but never enforced (Charge/Exceeded/ResetRound have zero production callers)
confirmed.evidence: budget.go:64-70 documents the enforcement contract: 'its runOnce path consults this tracker after a successful Acquire. When Exceeded() reports true the runner Releases the slot and emits cortex.lobe.budget_skipped'. LobeRunner has no tracker field and runOnce (lobe.go:249-291) never consults it. Grep across cmd/ + internal/ (tests excluded) shows Charge/Exceeded/ResetRound/RoundOutputBudget are referenced only inside budget.go itself. Cortex.Start registers a hub subscriber feeding RecordMainTurn (cortex.go:383-402), so data flows in but the cap gates nothing — LLM lobes can spend unbounded output tokens per round.
confirmed.fix: Wire the enforcement half per spec item 21: (1) add a tracker *BudgetTracker field to LobeRunner and a parameter to NewLobeRunner (lobe.go:152); pass c.tracker at the construction site cortex.go:233. (2) In runOnce (lobe.go:276-286), for KindLLM after a successful Acquire, if tracker != nil && tracker.Exceeded() then return early (the deferred sem.Release() frees the slot) after emitting a "cortex.lobe.budget_skipped" hub event with the lobe ID — matching the spec's Acquire-then-check ordering (cortex-core.md line 774, gotcha 7). (3) Call c.tracker.ResetRound() at the top of Cortex.MidturnNote (cortex.go:540) before the TickRound fan-out so each round starts with a zeroed accumulator. (4) Provide a Charge path: expose the tracker to lobes via LobeInput (or charge in the runner from a usage-returning Run variant) so future LLM lobes accumulate output tokens; today no production lobe is KindLLM so this is contract-completion, not behavior change. (5) Add a runner-level test: RecordMainTurn(0)+tick a KindLLM fake lobe → Run skipped + budget_skipped emitted; RecordMainTurn(1000) → Run invoked. Alternatively, if enforcement is deliberately deferred to LLM-lobe activation, the minimum honest fix is: correct docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:342 (cap does not exist yet), fix budget.go:64-70 ("wiring lives in lobe.go" is false), and un-mark spec item 21 / note the gap in specs/cortex-core.md STATUS. Preferred: implement the wiring (small, testable, all in-repo).
confirmed.verify_reason: All factual assertions verified at HEAD: LobeRunner (internal/cortex/lobe.go:110-135, 152-161) has no tracker field and runOnce (lobe.go:249-291) never consults BudgetTracker after Acquire; Charge/Exceeded/ResetRound/RoundOutputBudget have zero non-test callers (grep across cmd/+internal/); "cortex.lobe.budget_skipped" is emitted nowhere (only the budget.go:68 doc comment mentions it); the collection side IS live in production (cortex.go:383-402 subscriber, built per-run by engine/native_runner.go:611-648). One correction to the finder's failure scenario: unbounded LLM-lobe spend is NOT reachable at HEAD, because no KindLLM lobe is registered in production — native_runner.go:626-631 registers only the 4 deterministic lobes ("MVP"), and cmd/r1/mcp_serve_runtime.go:118-123 registers deterministic lobes with a stubProvider that errors on any LLM call, with --lobes=all documented RESERVED (mcp_serve_runtime.go:63-67). The finding still confirms as dormant/partial wiring rather than intentional design because specs/cortex-core.md is marked <!-- STATUS: done --> while its item 21 (line 851) explicitly requires the runOnce Exceeded-after-Acquire check + budget_skipped emission, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:342 asserts "Per-turn budget caps Lobe output at 30% of main-thread tokens" as an existing feature — both claims the code does not fulfill. budget.go:69-70 further claims "The wiring lives in lobe.go (TASK-9)", which is false. Consequence: the moment LLM lobes are activated (fully implemented, one plumbing step away), there is no cost cap and no budget_skipped telemetry despite spec/docs promising both; today every production cortex feeds a tracker whose enforcement half is dead code.

confirmed.title: seqAllocator.Stop can strand concurrent next() callers blocked forever on their reply channel
confirmed.evidence: next() checks quit only BEFORE enqueueing, then blocks unconditionally: `case a.requests <- reply: } ; return <-reply` (lines 96-101). run()'s select exits immediately on `<-a.quit` (line 73-74) without draining the buffered requests channel (cap 64). If Stop() closes quit while requests are pending (or the select randomly picks the quit branch when both are ready), the enqueued caller's `<-reply` never receives → permanent goroutine leak; a lane-event emitter (emitLaneEvent -> nextLaneSeq, lane_lifecycle.go:195-207) hangs while holding no way to recover. The doc claims 'Safe to call from any goroutine, including under concurrent next() pressure' (lines 104-106) — false.
confirmed.fix: In internal/cortex/seq_allocator.go: (1) run(): on <-a.quit, before returning, drain a.requests in a non-blocking loop and close() each drained reply channel (close = 'stopped' signal). (2) next(): after enqueueing, replace `return <-reply` with a select on `v, ok := <-reply` and `<-a.done`; on ok==false or done-with-empty-reply (do one final non-blocking reply read to catch a serviced-then-exited race), panic("cortex: seq allocator stopped") to honor the documented post-stop contract. This closes both strand windows: quit chosen over a buffered request, and enqueue landing after run() exited (next()'s send case can win the select even with quit closed). (3) Add a regression test: N goroutines loop next() (recovering the documented panic) while Stop() races; assert every caller returns or panics within a deadline (the current code fails this ~74% of the time per repro). Keep the Stop() doc as-is — fix the code to match it.
confirmed.verify_reason: Mechanism CONFIRMED empirically: reproduced with an exact copy of the allocator — Stop() concurrent with a single next() stranded the caller (no return, no panic) in 1486/2000 iterations. Code evidence: internal/cortex/seq_allocator.go:94-101 (next() checks quit only pre-enqueue, then blocks unconditionally on <-reply) and :71-83 (run() exits on <-a.quit without draining the cap-64 requests buffer; select picks randomly when both cases are ready). The doc contract at seq_allocator.go:104-106 ('Safe to call from any goroutine, including under concurrent next() pressure') is false, and next()'s documented panic-after-stop (lines 90-93) is violated — it hangs instead. SEVERITY CAVEAT (downgrade from implied P1 to P2): the finder's production scenario (lane emitter hang via emitLaneEvent→nextLaneSeq) cannot occur at HEAD. Repo-wide grep shows a.Stop() is reachable only via Workspace.StopSeqAllocator (seq_allocator.go:144-152), whose sole caller is seq_allocator_test.go:121, deferred after all next() calls have quiesced; the three direct test Stop() calls are likewise sequenced after quiescence; Cortex.Stop (cortex.go:463) never calls it and the doc says production lets the goroutine outlive the Workspace. So this is a proven latent race + false documented API contract in an exported 'graceful shutdown' method — the first future caller that wires it under load deadlocks a lane emitter goroutine permanently. In-scope (correctness bug + docs claiming what code doesn't do) and trivially fixable in-repo.
