confirmed.title: Ledger WriteNode: non-atomic two-tier write + chain-presence dedup permanently loses node content on crash
confirmed.evidence: WriteNode writes the chain tier first via plain `os.WriteFile(chainPath, chainData, 0o600)` (store.go:133), then the content tier (store.go:144). Neither write is tmp+rename atomic. The dedup guard at store.go:112-117 returns early when the chain file exists: "Chain record already exists; treat as dedup. Do NOT touch the content tier either — we can't distinguish 'previously redacted' from 'never written'". So a crash or disk-full between the chain write and the content write leaves a chain record with no content; any retry of AddNode/Batch (which are documented as idempotent-by-dedup, store.go:104-106) is a silent no-op and the content is unrecoverable — indistinguishable from a crypto-shred (redact.go:101-120 will report the node as redacted). Additionally a torn chain JSON from the non-atomic write makes ReadNode fail (store.go:197-198), which turns EVERY Ledger.Query into a hard 'integrity violation' error (ledger.go:407-408), while ListNodes/ListEdges silently skip the corrupt file (store.go:266-268, 286-292) so RebuildIndex silently drops it.
confirmed.fix: In internal/ledger/store.go: (1) add an atomicWriteFile helper (write to a .tmp file in the same directory, f.Sync(), close, os.Rename onto the final path); use it for the chain record (store.go:133), content record (store.go:144), WriteContentBlob (store.go:183), and WriteEdge (store.go:248). (2) Reorder WriteNode to write the content tier BEFORE the chain record so chain-file presence becomes the commit point and the dedup guard at store.go:112 stays sound; on chain-write failure, best-effort os.Remove the just-written content file so no orphan content blob lingers. (3) In ReadNode, map a zero-length or unmarshal-failing chain file to a distinct sentinel error (e.g. ErrCorruptChainRecord wrapping the ID) so Ledger.Query (ledger.go:403-408) can report the specific corrupt node instead of a generic integrity violation — keep the fail-loud behavior, just make it diagnosable. (4) Tests: write a truncated chain file + durable index row and assert Query surfaces the named corrupt-record error; make the content dir unwritable and assert WriteNode leaves no chain record behind (i.e., a subsequent WriteNode with the same ID succeeds and persists content). Do NOT change the dedup guard's refusal to resurrect content — that is correct for redaction; content-first ordering removes the case it could mask.
confirmed.verify_reason: Core mechanism verified, headline consequence overstated. VERIFIED: WriteNode writes chain then content via plain os.WriteFile with no tmp+rename/fsync (internal/ledger/store.go:133,144; also WriteContentBlob:183, WriteEdge:248); dedup guard returns early on chain-file presence without repairing content (store.go:112-117); torn/empty chain JSON makes ReadNode fail (store.go:197-198) which turns matching Ledger.Query calls into hard "integrity violation" errors (ledger.go:407-408, also 486-489), while ListNodes/RebuildIndex silently skip/drop it (store.go:266-268); chain-without-content is by design indistinguishable from crypto-shred (redact.go:94-96, verify.go never reads content). The SQLite index IS fsync-durable (WAL, default synchronous) while chain files are not, so after power loss a durable index row can reference a torn/zero-length chain file — a concrete, reachable failure. Crash/ENOSPC between the two writes leaves a permanent phantom "redacted" chain record in an audit ledger. REFUTED PRONG: "any retry of AddNode/Batch is a silent no-op, content unrecoverable" is wrong — AddNode (ledger.go:280-290) and Batch (ledger.go:551-561) generate a fresh random salt per call, so retries compute a different node ID and cannot hit the dedup guard; no production caller pre-supplies Salt/ContentCommitment. The only same-ID writers are the migration import (cmd/r1-server/migrate_in.go:248,293), which self-repairs via WriteContentBlob's idempotent overwrite (store.go:173-183), and PersistPackAdopted (pack_adopted_event.go:95-118) whose deriveAdoptNodeID includes a second-granularity timestamp (cmd/r1/pack_adopt_cmd.go:190) — only a same-second retry collides. Net: real crash-consistency defect in the audit ledger's persistence layer with user-visible consequences (bricked Query after power loss; permanent phantom-redacted nodes), fix is small and local, but severity is lower than the finder implies because the dedup-retry data-loss path is essentially unreachable in production.

confirmed.title: Ledger.Batch claims 'all operations succeed or none do' but has no rollback — failed batches persist partial graphs
confirmed.evidence: Doc comment ledger.go:510-511: "Batch atomically writes multiple nodes and edges. All operations succeed or none do." But Phase 2 (ledger.go:583-593) writes+indexes every node immediately, and Phase 3 (ledger.go:596-615) only then validates edge endpoints: `if _, err := l.store.ReadNode(it.edge.From); err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("ledger: batch edge from %q not found...") }`. A batch [AddNode A, AddEdge A→missing] returns an error yet node A is permanently persisted in both the store and the SQLite index; no compensation/rollback exists. Same for a mid-batch WriteNode/InsertNode failure (disk full): earlier nodes stay committed.
confirmed.fix: Do NOT implement rollback-by-deletion — the store is append-only by design and WriteNode explicitly cannot distinguish "previously redacted" from "never written" (store.go:113-115), so deleting chain/content files conflicts with the design. Instead: (1) Move the edge-endpoint existence checks from Phase 3 (ledger.go:598-607) into Phase 1: Phase 1 already computes each new node's final ID (line 561), so build the newNodeIDs set during Phase 1 and validate every BatchAddEdge From/To against newNodeIDs plus l.store.ReadNode BEFORE any write. All validation failures then leave the ledger untouched. (2) Rewrite the doc comment at 510-511 to the honest contract: all operations are validated up front and validation failures write nothing; a mid-batch I/O failure (e.g. disk full) may leave earlier operations persisted, and replay is idempotent only when the caller pre-supplies Salt/ContentCommitment (content-addressed dedup). (3) Add a test: Batch([AddNode A, AddEdge A->nonexistent]) must return an error AND QueryNodes/ReadNode must show A absent.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at internal/ledger/ledger.go:510-618. Doc comment (lines 510-511) promises "All operations succeed or none do", but Phase 2 (583-593) persists every node to the filesystem store AND SQLite index before Phase 3 (596-615) validates edge endpoints; no rollback exists. A batch [AddNode A, AddEdge A->missing] returns an error yet leaves A permanently in the graph — reachable via the exported API (TestBatchRejectsEdgeToNonexistent at ledger_test.go:580 exercises exactly this path but never asserts atomicity; TestBatchAtomicNodeAndEdges tests only the success path despite its name). The "replay is idempotent" defense in store.go:105-106 does not refute it: with Salt=="" Phase 1 (ledger.go:551-561) generates a fresh random salt and computeID (216-238) hashes the salt-dependent commitment, so retrying a failed batch creates a DUPLICATE node under a new ID rather than deduping, and a permanently-invalid batch has no successful replay at all — orphans stay forever. Mitigating factor lowering severity: Ledger.Batch/BatchOp have zero non-test callers in cmd/ or internal/, so no shipped code path hits it today; it is a latent contract bug in an exported, documented, tested governance-ledger API ("docs that claim things the code doesn't do").

confirmed.title: atomicfs.Transaction.Commit rollback leaves newly-created files on disk, violating the multi-file atomicity contract
confirmed.evidence: Package doc (transaction.go:9): "Multi-file atomicity: all changes apply or none do". But rollback (transaction.go:251-257) only restores backups of files that pre-existed (`for _, b := range backups { os.WriteFile(b.path, b.data, 0644) }`) and removes leftover temp files; files whose rename already succeeded and had no original (opKindCreate, or opKindWrite to a new path) are never deleted. Failure scenario: tx.Create("a.txt"); tx.Create("b/c.txt"); rename of the second fails (permission/EXDEV/dir-appeared) → Commit returns error but a.txt remains on disk. Secondary: Phase-3 backup silently skips files whose ReadFile fails (transaction.go:242-246, `if err == nil` only), so rollback then cannot restore them, and rollback's os.WriteFile errors are ignored (transaction.go:254).
confirmed.fix: In internal/atomicfs/transaction.go Commit(): (1) Phase 4 — track successfully renamed staged entries (e.g. `var renamed []staged`); in rollback(), iterate `renamed` and for ops with origExists==false call os.Remove(s.op.Path) (backups already cover origExists==true); keep cleanup() for un-renamed temps. (2) Phase 3 — if op.origExists and os.ReadFile(op.Path) fails, abort Commit with an error (after cleanup()) instead of silently skipping, since rollback would otherwise be unable to restore that file. (3) Collect rollback os.WriteFile/os.Remove errors and append them to the returned Commit error (best-effort rollback must at least surface failures). Optionally fsync temp files before rename for crash safety. Add regression tests mirroring the two repros: multi-Create with rename collision (Create "d/inner.txt" then Create "d") and Create+Delete-of-non-empty-dir; assert no created files survive a failed Commit.
confirmed.verify_reason: CONFIRMED by deterministic reproduction. I copied a repro test into internal/atomicfs and ran it: (1) tx.Create("d/inner.txt") + tx.Create("d") in one transaction — Phase 2 MkdirAll creates dir "d", Phase 4 rename of "d" fails ("file exists"), Commit returns error, but d/inner.txt REMAINS on disk; (2) tx.Create("brandnew.txt") + tx.Delete(nonEmptyDir) — all renames succeed, delete fails ("directory not empty"), Commit errors, but brandnew.txt REMAINS. Both violate the documented contract (transaction.go:9 "Multi-file atomicity: all changes apply or none do"). Code reading confirms the mechanism: rollback (transaction.go:251-257) only restores `backups` (populated solely for ops with origExists==true, lines 240-247) and removes temp paths via cleanup (lines 205-209); once a temp is renamed into place, os.Remove(tmpPath) is a silent ENOENT no-op and nothing removes op.Path for creates/new-path writes. Secondary claims verified: Phase 3 silently skips unreadable originals (`if err == nil` only, line 243) making later rollback impossible for them, and rollback ignores os.WriteFile errors (line 254). One finder inaccuracy: EXDEV cannot trigger this since temps are created in the target's own directory (line 218) — immaterial, other triggers demonstrated. Severity tempered from implied P1 to P2 because no current production caller reaches the broken path: worktree/helpers.go:391-401 only calls Validate(), and deploy WriteIfAbsent commits single-op transactions. Existing tests (TestMultiFileAtomicCommit etc.) cover only the happy path.

confirmed.title: session.Store.SaveAttempt silently discards unreadable attempt history and overwrites it, resetting attempt numbering
confirmed.evidence: SaveAttempt ignores the read error: `s.readJSON(path, &attempts)` (store.go:202) — if history/<task>.json exists but fails to parse (corrupt file, wrong shape, permission error), `attempts` stays nil, the new attempt is appended to an empty slice, and writeJSON (store.go:213) atomically replaces the file with a single-element array — silently destroying all prior attempt history. NextAttemptNumber (store.go:191-194) swallows the same error (`prior, _ := store.LoadAttempts(taskID)`) and returns 1, so retry intelligence (failure escalation, learned patterns keyed off prev attempt at store.go:206-211) silently resets. Callers in cmd/r1/main.go:514/530/1486/1492 also drop SaveAttempt's error, so nothing surfaces.
confirmed.fix: In Store.SaveAttempt (internal/session/store.go:202), capture the readJSON error and branch: if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err), quarantine the unreadable file by renaming it to history/<task>.json.corrupt (preserving evidence), log a warning, and proceed with a fresh slice — or return fmt.Errorf("read attempt history %s: %w", path, err). If returning the error, also surface it at the four call sites that drop it (cmd/r1/main.go:514, 530, 1486, 1492), otherwise the fix stays silent. Apply the same IsNotExist distinction where LoadAttempts errors are blanked at main.go:496 and 1482. Additionally either delete the dead NextAttemptNumber helper (store.go:189-194) or make main.go use it so the logic lives in one place. Add a regression test: write garbage to history/T1.json, call SaveAttempt, assert the old file is quarantined/error returned rather than silently replaced.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified in current tree: internal/session/store.go:202 discards readJSON's error in SaveAttempt, and store.go:213 atomically rewrites history/<task>.json with only the new attempt — so an existing-but-unparseable/unreadable history file (zero-length file after power loss since writeAtomicJSON never fsyncs, EACCES file in writable dir, hand edit, schema drift) is silently truncated to one attempt. This is a bug, not design: LoadAttempts (store.go:220-223) explicitly distinguishes IsNotExist from real errors and propagates them, and SQLStore.SaveAttempt (sqlstore.go:152) appends rows and cannot truncate, so the two SessionStore implementations diverge. User-visible: cmd/r1/main.go:496-497 and 1482-1483 then compute attemptNum=1 and display it via ui.TaskComplete/SendTaskComplete, and the learning extraction at store.go:206-211 loses its previous-attempt lookup — all with zero log output since main.go:514/530/1486/1492 drop SaveAttempt errors. Tests (store_test.go) cover only happy path and missing file. Minor claim correction: NextAttemptNumber (store.go:191) has no callers anywhere — it is dead code — but the identical inline pattern in main.go is live, so the substance holds. Severity moderated to P3: trigger is narrow (atomic tmp+rename writes make corruption rare) and the destroyed data is retry metadata, not user code or session state.

confirmed.title: checkpoint.PruneTimelineAfter ignores write/close errors then renames a possibly-truncated file over the authoritative WAL
confirmed.evidence: The WAL rewrite loop drops all errors: `for _, e := range keep { b, _ := json.Marshal(e); f.Write(b); f.Write([]byte{'\n'}) }; f.Close(); return os.Rename(tmp, p)` (resume.go:201-207). If the disk fills or an I/O error occurs mid-write, f.Write returns an error that is discarded, f.Close's flush error is discarded, and the truncated .prune-tmp is renamed over timeline.jsonl — silently corrupting/losing checkpoint history that --resume-from depends on (including possibly the target checkpoint itself). This contradicts the package's own design goal of an fsync-protected append-only WAL (timeline.go:11-13, 145-146).
confirmed.fix: In PruneTimelineAfter (internal/checkpoint/resume.go), check every error in the rewrite: for each entry, handle json.Marshal error and check both f.Write calls (or build the full buffer and do one checked Write); then call f.Sync() and f.Close(), checking both. On any failure: f.Close() if still open, os.Remove(tmp), and return a wrapped error WITHOUT renaming, leaving the original timeline.jsonl intact (the caller at cmd/r1/main.go:2030 already degrades gracefully by warning and continuing). Also os.Remove(tmp) if os.Rename fails, to avoid leaking .prune-tmp. Optionally add a test that pre-creates the checkpoints path as unwritable or injects a write failure to assert the original WAL survives a failed prune.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at internal/checkpoint/resume.go:196-207: PruneTimelineAfter discards every f.Write error, never calls f.Sync, discards f.Close's error, then unconditionally os.Rename's the tmp file over .stoke/checkpoints/timeline.jsonl. On ENOSPC/EIO mid-write the rename still typically succeeds (same-directory metadata op), silently replacing the WAL with a truncated file. This contradicts the package's own documented design (timeline.go:8-17 'fsync-on-write' WAL; Timeline.Checkpoint at timeline.go:142-146 checks write errors and fsyncs). Concrete user-visible consequence: checkpoint history is silently lost, so a later `stoke sow --resume-from CP-NNN` fails with 'checkpoint not found in WAL' and exits 1; additionally NewTimeline (timeline.go:109-115) counts newlines for the CP sequence and appends, so a partial trailing line causes the next checkpoint to concatenate into malformed JSON that ListCheckpoints silently skips — corruption compounds. The sole caller (cmd/r1/main.go:2030) treats prune errors as a non-fatal warning, but no error is ever surfaced. Test coverage (resume_test.go:89-109) is happy-path only. Mitigants: the in-flight resume itself is unaffected (ResumeState is built before pruning), only .stoke metadata is at risk, and --fresh recovers — hence P2, not P1.

confirmed.title: session.Journal is dormant and its Rotate() corrupts sequence numbering by swallowing write/close/rename errors
confirmed.evidence: No production caller constructs a Journal (grep for NewJournal outside internal/session finds only tests). Within it, Rotate() ignores every error: `j.file.Write(data)` (journal.go:156), `j.file.Close()` (158), `os.Rename(j.path, segPath)` (163). If the rename fails, the code reopens the SAME path with O_APPEND and resets `j.seq = 0` (journal.go:166-171) — subsequent entries are appended to the same file with duplicate/decreasing seq values, breaking replay ordering; if OpenFile fails, j.file keeps pointing at the closed handle. Separately, countLines (journal.go:241-253) uses a default 64KB bufio.Scanner while Append has no line-size limit and Replay allows 1MB (journal.go:185) — a >64KB tool-result entry makes countLines stop early on reopen, so seq restarts low and duplicates existing seq numbers, violating the append-only WAL invariant claimed at journal.go:1-7.
confirmed.fix: Delete internal/session/journal.go and internal/session/journal_test.go — internal/journal is the live, doc-referenced session journal (journal.ndjson via sessionhub), and this .jsonl variant is an unwired duplicate. Deletion is preferred over repair; if the team instead wants to keep it for future wiring, then: (1) in Rotate(), check and propagate errors from j.file.Write, j.file.Close, and os.Rename, aborting rotation (keeping the old handle, path, and seq) on any failure so seq never resets against an un-renamed file; (2) give countLines the same 1MB scanner.Buffer as Replay and check scanner.Err(); (3) add a test appending a >64KB entry then reopening to lock the seq-continuation invariant. Verify with go build ./cmd/r1 && go test ./internal/session/... && go vet ./internal/session/....
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at HEAD: internal/session/journal.go exports NewJournal/Journal/Replay/ReplayFiltered/JournalEntry with zero production references — only internal/session/journal_test.go uses them. The production session journal is a different package (internal/journal, writing journal.ndjson, wired via internal/server/sessionhub/reload.go:44 through the sessionhub.Journal interface at sessionhub/session.go:170, which session.Journal's signature does not satisfy), so this file is a dormant duplicate. The internal bugs are also real: Rotate() discards errors from Write (journal.go:156), Close (:158), and Rename (:163); on rename failure it reopens the same path with O_APPEND and resets seq=0 (:166-171), producing duplicate/decreasing seq values in one file, violating the append-only ordering invariant claimed at journal.go:1-7. countLines (:241-253) uses a default 64KB bufio.Scanner with scanner.Err() ignored while Append has no line cap and Replay allows 1MB (:185), so a >64KB entry silently truncates the count on reopen and seq restarts low — exactly the invariant journal_test.go:126-150 asserts. Minor correction to the claim: if the reopen in Rotate fails, the error IS returned and later Appends fail loudly with os.ErrClosed, so that sub-point is partially mitigated. Because nothing constructs Journal in production, there is no current user-visible runtime failure — the concrete consequence is dead code duplicating the live internal/journal system with latent seq-corruption bugs, so severity is P3, not higher.

confirmed.title: patchapply concurrent-edit detection is advisory-only and computes the wrong line number, and Apply itself is dormant
confirmed.evidence: The hashline guard appends "concurrent edit detected" to result.Errors (patch.go:250-253) but never skips the file: execution falls through to applyHunks and os.WriteFile (patch.go:265-280), the file is overwritten and reported in result.Applied — so the detection cannot prevent anything. The line-number math is also wrong: `lineNum := h.OldStart + i` (patch.go:248) iterates i over ALL hunk lines including '+' additions, which do not consume old-file lines, and double-counts OldStart's own line (first context line should be OldStart+0 only if adds are excluded) — producing spurious mismatch reports on valid patches and missing real ones. Only patchapply.Parse is used in production (internal/workflow/workflow.go:1764 for stats); Apply/ApplyReverse/DryRun have no non-test callers.
confirmed.fix: In internal/patchapply/patch.go applyPatch: preferred option (a) — delete the hashline pre-check block (lines 239-257) and its hashline import, since findMatch already enforces exact context/delete-line matching at the apply position (the actual concurrency guard); update the package doc comment to say context matching in findMatch is the concurrent-edit protection, and add a regression test asserting a valid patch with additions yields len(result.Errors)==0. Option (b) if hashline verification must be kept: track old-file position with a dedicated counter incremented only for OpContext/OpDelete lines (lineNum := h.OldStart + oldConsumed, then oldConsumed++), perform the check at the fuzzy-matched position rather than fixed OldStart (or accept ±3 false positives), and on mismatch append to result.Failed and continue to the next file BEFORE applyHunks/WriteFile so DryRun and Apply both refuse the file. Either way, extend patch_test.go to assert Errors is empty on clean applies. Severity P2 (not P1): the broken guard sits in dormant code — Apply/ApplyReverse/DryRun have no production callers today — so there is no live corruption path, but the repo ships a falsely-advertised safety mechanism with tests that mask it.
confirmed.verify_reason: All three core claims verified against the working tree and empirically. (1) Advisory-only: internal/patchapply/patch.go:242-257 appends "concurrent edit detected" to result.Errors with no continue/Failed marking; flow proceeds to applyHunks (line 265), os.WriteFile (line 274), and result.Applied (line 280). Demonstrated with a temporary test (removed after): Applied=[f.txt] alongside 3 mismatch errors. (2) Line math wrong: lineNum := h.OldStart + i (line 248) indexes over all hunk lines including OpAdd, which consume no old-file lines; a valid patch whose file exactly matched the diff produced spurious mismatches at lines 6/7/8 (true lines 5/6/7), and inflated lineNums past EOF are silently skipped (GetTag ok=false), so real edits at trailing context lines are never checked — including in the package's own sampleDiff test fixture. One evidence correction: there is no "double-count of OldStart's own line" — hashline.GetTag is 1-indexed (hashline.go:94-99) so OldStart+0 is correct for the first old line; the only bug is counting '+' lines. (3) Dormancy: repo-wide grep shows the sole non-test caller is patchapply.Parse at internal/workflow/workflow.go:1764 (Stats for a retry prompt); Apply/ApplyReverse/DryRun have zero production callers, and patch_test.go (lines 66-106) never asserts Errors is empty, which is why the noise is invisible to CI. Additional nuance: even with corrected math the pre-check is redundant — findMatch (patch.go:354-380) requires exact equality of context+delete lines, so a real concurrent edit already fails the apply (verified: file went to Failed, untouched), while a legitimate ±3 fuzzy shift would still false-positive a fixed-position hashline check. User-visible consequence: the package doc (patch.go:1-11) and CLAUDE.md advertise concurrent-edit verification that is decorative and noisy; any future wiring of Apply gets an ApplyResult whose Errors field is polluted on ordinary add-containing patches and whose "detection" never blocks a write.

confirmed.title: patchapply.ApplyReverse cannot undo file creations or deletions — falls through to the modify path with /dev/null paths
confirmed.evidence: The package doc promises "Reverse application (undo a patch)" (patch.go:10). applyPatch only special-cases `fp.IsNew && !reverse` (patch.go:200) and `fp.IsDelete && !reverse` (patch.go:212). With reverse=true, an IsNew patch falls to the generic branch where `path = fp.OldPath` == "/dev/null" (patch.go:227-232), so os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, "/dev/null")) fails and the created file is never removed; reversing an IsDelete patch similarly targets NewPath=="/dev/null" instead of recreating OldPath. Undo of any patch that adds or deletes files is silently a Failed entry. (Dormant: ApplyReverse has no production callers.)
confirmed.fix: In applyPatch (internal/patchapply/patch.go), normalize reverse patches before dispatch instead of adding parallel branches: at the top of the per-file loop, if reverse, transform fp — swap OldPath/NewPath, swap IsNew/IsDelete, and set fp.Hunks = reverseHunks(fp.Hunks) — then run the existing forward logic with reverse-independent guards (`fp.IsNew` creates via applyNewFile, `fp.IsDelete` removes via os.Remove, else modify without re-reversing hunks). This makes reverse-of-create remove NewPath and reverse-of-delete recreate OldPath from the hunk's delete/context lines (reverseHunks already flips OpDelete->OpAdd so applyNewFile works unchanged), respecting dryRun in both cases. Alternatively (smaller diff): add explicit `fp.IsNew && reverse` (os.Remove(NewPath), tolerate IsNotExist) and `fp.IsDelete && reverse` (mirror applyNewFile collecting OpDelete|OpContext lines into OldPath) branches. Add two tests mirroring TestApplyNewFile/TestApplyDeleteFile that Apply then ApplyReverse and assert the filesystem is restored (created file removed; deleted file recreated with original content), plus DryRun-reverse assertions that nothing is touched.
confirmed.verify_reason: Empirically reproduced both failure modes with a throwaway test in internal/patchapply. (1) Reversing an IsNew patch: applyPatch only guards `fp.IsNew && !reverse` (patch.go:200), so with reverse=true it falls to the generic path where path=fp.OldPath=="/dev/null" (patch.go:227-229); os.ReadFile(root+"/dev/null") fails and the created file stays on disk (repro: failed=[/dev/null], new.go still exists). (2) Reversing an IsDelete patch: minor correction to the finder's evidence — the reverse path targets fp.OldPath (the real path), not NewPath=="/dev/null" — but the outcome matches the claim: the file was deleted by forward application, ReadFile fails, and the file is never recreated (repro: failed=[old.go], not recreated). Package doc (patch.go:10) promises "Reverse application (undo a patch)" and ApplyReverse (patch.go:187) is exported, so the documented contract is unmet for create/delete patches. Existing TestApplyReverse (patch_test.go:108) only covers modify patches. Mitigations that cap severity: the failure is reported in ApplyResult.Failed/Errors (not fully silent, though the "/dev/null" error is misleading), and ApplyReverse has zero production callers — the only production use of the package is Parse+Stats in internal/workflow/workflow.go:1764 — so no live pipeline is affected today.

confirmed.title: snapshot.minLen is inverted (returns max) — Summary never truncates and Summary/Diff panic on commits shorter than 8 chars
confirmed.evidence: `func minLen(a, b int) int { if a < b { return b } return a }` (workspace.go:212-217) returns the MAXIMUM. Summary's `s.Commit[:minLen(8, len(s.Commit))]` (workspace.go:208) therefore slices to max(8, len): for a normal 40-char SHA it prints the full SHA (guard is a no-op), and for any Commit shorter than 8 (zero-value Snapshot, truncated/hand-edited snapshot JSON via Load at workspace.go:124-134) it evaluates Commit[:8] and panics with slice bounds out of range. Diff has the same unguarded panic at workspace.go:178 (`a.Commit[:8]`).
confirmed.fix: In internal/snapshot/workspace.go: (1) delete minLen and use the Go builtin min (go.mod declares go 1.25.5) — Summary becomes s.Commit[:min(8, len(s.Commit))]; (2) guard Diff the same way: fmt.Sprintf("commit: %s → %s", a.Commit[:min(8, len(a.Commit))], b.Commit[:min(8, len(b.Commit))]); (3) strengthen workspace_test.go TestSummary to assert the short-SHA truncation (40-char commit renders 8-char prefix) and add a short-commit case (e.g. Commit "abc" and Commit "") for both Summary and Diff so the regression cannot recur silently.
confirmed.verify_reason: Reproduced both claimed mechanics against the working tree: minLen at internal/snapshot/workspace.go:212-217 returns the maximum (verified minLen(8,40)==40 via a throwaway test), so Summary (workspace.go:208) never truncates a 40-char SHA and panics 'slice bounds out of range [:8] with length 3' on any Commit shorter than 8 (zero-value Snapshot or unvalidated Load() JSON, workspace.go:124-134); Diff (workspace.go:178) has the same unguarded [:8]. TestSummary (workspace_test.go:112-124) masks the bug by using a 12-char commit and asserting only non-empty output. One refinement: repo-wide grep shows the only production importers of internal/snapshot are workflow.go (Take/Restore) and wizard/init.go (Take/Save) — nothing calls Summary() or Diff() — so the panic is latent in dormant exported API rather than reachable via current CLI wiring, which lowers severity but does not refute the defect: the exported API violates its evident contract, and the covering test is dishonest per the audit brief.

confirmed.title: memory.Store.RememberWithContext has a lock-gap race that mutates and returns the wrong entry under concurrency
confirmed.evidence: RememberWithContext calls s.Remember (which locks, appends, unlocks) and then re-acquires the lock and assumes the last element is its own entry: `s.mu.Lock(); idx := len(s.entries) - 1; s.entries[idx].Context = context; s.entries[idx].File = file; return &s.entries[idx]` (memory.go:109-116). If another goroutine's Remember interleaves between the two critical sections, Context/File are written onto the OTHER goroutine's entry and the wrong *Entry is returned. Store is explicitly concurrency-safe (sync.RWMutex, memory.go:52) and has concurrent production callers: the MCP memory tool (internal/tools/memory_tools.go:68) and the cortex memorycurator lobe (internal/cortex/lobes/memorycurator/curate.go:154). Rewrite Remember and RememberWithContext to each acquire s.mu once, call rememberLocked with all fields, and return a copy of the entry (change signatures to return Entry, or keep *Entry but return a pointer to a heap copy, never &s.entries[i]) so callers hold no alias into the slice. confirmed.title: research Orchestrator: subagent write failures are swallowed while the Lead deliberately prefers disk — findings silently vanish from synthesis

confirmed.title: r1-browser doc claims Google JWKS signature verification; verifyBearer only checks token shape

IAM is the actual gate (comment :129-133).

Optionally add that last warning to the supervisor.go:149 comment as well. (Alternative — implementing in-app JWKS verification — is larger and contradicts the documented v1 decision; the doc fix is the minimal correct change.)
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified by reading the code: services/r1-browser/main.go:22-25 claims the service verifies Google-signed ID tokens via the JWKS endpoint https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs cached for an hour, but verifyBearer (supervisor.go:134-152) only checks the 'Bearer ' prefix, len>=16, and 3 dot-segments — no signature/audience/expiry verification — and R1_BROWSER_DEV_ANY_BEARER (supervisor.go:149) accepts arbitrary non-JWT strings. Concrete consequence: an operator/security reviewer relying on the package doc would believe the app self-verifies tokens and could relax ingress/invoker settings, when any 16+ char 3-segment string passes (main_test.go:62 asserts exactly this).

confirmed.title: cloudbuild-r1-browser smoke curls run.app /livez unauthenticated but the service is deployed no-allow-unauthenticated + internal ingress — smoke can never pass
confirmed.evidence: Deploy uses `--no-allow-unauthenticated` (:58) and `--ingress=internal-and-cloud-load-balancing` (:69); the smoke step comments "/livez is unauthenticated (it's outside the WS path)" (:84) and curls the default URL with no identity token (:86). Cloud Run IAM/ingress rejects before the container sees the request (403/404), so the pipeline's final step always fails.
confirmed.fix: Replace the data-plane curl in the smoke step (services/cloudbuild-r1-browser.yaml:74-95) with a control-plane readiness assertion that works regardless of ingress/IAM: poll `gcloud run services describe r1-browser-${_ENV} --region=${_REGION} --format='value(status.conditions[0].status)'` for Ready=True, and assert the serving revision runs the new image, e.g. compare `gcloud run services describe ... --format='value(status.latestReadyRevisionName)'` against `status.traffic` and verify the revision's image tag equals $SHORT_SHA via `gcloud run revisions describe`. Also fix the misleading :84 comment (Cloud Run IAM applies to /livez too). Alternative (only if data-plane smoke is required): configure a VPC-connected private worker pool via `options.pool` AND add `-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=$URL)"` — note the auth header alone cannot work because internal ingress rejects default-pool Cloud Build traffic with 404 before IAM runs; relaxing ingress to `all` would contradict the documented security design (docs/operations/r1-browser-service.md:35-36, spec §T10). The pool creation itself is operator infra, which is why the control-plane check is the preferred in-repo fix.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at services/cloudbuild-r1-browser.yaml: deploy uses --no-allow-unauthenticated (:58) and --ingress=internal-and-cloud-load-balancing (:69), while the smoke step curls the default run.app URL with no identity token (:86) from a default-pool Cloud Build worker (no options.pool configured, :26-28). Two independent platform barriers guarantee non-200: internal ingress returns 404 to external callers before the container is reached, and even inside the VPC, Cloud Run IAM returns 403 on ALL paths without a run.invoker identity token — the :84 comment ('/livez is unauthenticated') conflates app-level Bearer auth (only the CDP proxy at '/' requires Bearer, services/r1-browser/main.go:29-31,88-93) with platform IAM, which has no path exemptions. The 'dormant config' defense fails: docs/operations/r1-browser-service.md:92-95 instructs operators to run this exact config via gcloud builds submit for staging and prod promotion, so the guaranteed-failing smoke is the documented final gate of a real workflow. Not handled elsewhere: the pattern was copied from services/cloudbuild-deploy.yaml (:284-313) where it works only because those services deploy --allow-unauthenticated (:123,161,197,238). Concrete consequence: every run of the documented promotion pipeline ends red at the final step even though the deploy succeeded, training operators to ignore failing builds or blocking promotion. One correction to the finder: their suggested auth-header fix is insufficient alone — internal ingress 404s the Cloud Build worker before IAM is evaluated, so the token never gets a chance to matter.

confirmed.title: downloads-cdn '/…/sha256' endpoint returns md5+crc32c and no sha256
confirmed.evidence: Doc (:14) advertises `GET /<channel>/<asset>/sha256`, but the handler writes `{"ok":true,"object":...,"size":...,"md5":...,"crc32c":...}` (:158-166) — no sha256 field exists. Any install script doing `curl .../r1-linux-amd64/sha256` to verify a download gets checksums it didn't ask for.
confirmed.fix: In the wantSha branch of handleObject (main.go:158-166), stream-hash the object server-side: open obj.NewReader(ctx), io.Copy into crypto/sha256, and add "sha256":"<hex>" to the JSON response alongside md5/crc32c; set Cache-Control: public, max-age=300 to amortize the read (assets are <=~64MiB, objectViewer suffices, and the JSON stays tiny so the Cloud Run 32MiB response limit is irrelevant). Update the endpoint doc at main.go:14 and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:532 to state the full response shape. Optionally also emit sha256 sidecar metadata from cloudbuild-binaries.yaml for future objects, but the server-side hash is the complete in-repo fix. Add a handler-level test using a fake reader if the storage client is wrapped behind an interface; otherwise document the branch as GCS-integration-only.
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at services/r1-downloads-cdn/main.go: line 14 advertises `GET /<channel>/<asset>/sha256`, line 136 routes it, and lines 158-166 respond with only {ok, object, size, md5, crc32c} — no sha256 field. GCS ObjectAttrs carries no SHA256, the handler never reads attrs.Metadata, and neither release pipeline attaches one (cloudbuild-binaries.yaml:57-60 uploads raw binaries with no checksums; cloudbuild-release.yaml:46 puts checksums.txt only under the TAG prefix, not the prod/staging/dev channels this service serves). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:532 also advertises the endpoint. Concrete consequence: any external consumer curling downloads.r1.run/prod/r1-linux-amd64/sha256 to verify a download receives md5+crc32c it didn't ask for and cannot verify integrity via sha256 at all — the endpoint name is a false promise. Mitigations that lower severity but do not refute: the repo's own install.sh (lines 96-110) verifies via GitHub releases checksums.txt, and no in-repo client calls the endpoint, so nothing in-repo breaks today.

confirmed.title: Panels have no error handling for RPC failures, contradicting desktop-rpc's claim of graceful 'coming soon' rendering
confirmed.evidence: loadCost awaits invokeStub("cost_get_current"...) (:57-62) with no try/catch; same for ledger-viewer.ts:56, memory-inspector.ts:105, descent-ladder.ts:108 (grep shows the only try/catch in panels are session-view.ts:978 and skill-catalog.ts:513). cmd/r1/desktop_rpc_cmd.go:17-18 claims "The Tauri host handles the not_implemented error code gracefully by rendering a 'coming soon' state in the affected panel" — no panel does; rejections are unhandled and the cost panel keeps showing seeded $0.00.

Add vitest coverage by making the stub path throwable (inject a rejecting invoke) to assert the unavailable state renders. (b) Correct the stale header claim at cmd/r1/desktop_rpc_cmd.go:17-18 to describe actual behavior (panels render an unavailable state on not_implemented) once (a) makes a graceful state real — do not leave the comment claiming the Tauri host does this, since the host propagates errors verbatim (subprocess.rs:231).
confirmed.verify_reason: Verified end-to-end. (1) desktop_rpc_cmd.go:85 wires desktopapi.NotImplemented{} for all verbs, so cost.get_current/ledger.list_events/memory.list_scopes/descent.current_tier return -32010 not_implemented in every real session. (2) The Rust host propagates the error: ipc.rs:302-325 returns Err (also not_found when no session), and subprocess.rs:231 maps the wire error body to Err(IpcError) — no softening, no coming-soon rendering anywhere (grep: string absent from frontend). (3) cost-panel.ts:55-64, ledger-viewer.ts:56, memory-inspector.ts:104, descent-ladder.ts:103-114 all await invokeStub with no try/catch and are called fire-and-forget (void loadCost(root) etc.); main.ts has no unhandledrejection handler. confirmed.fix: Drop the desktop lane from the fix (it already exists). For services, add `RUN go test ./... -count=1 -timeout=120s` to the builder stage of each services/<svc>/Dockerfile (r1-admin, r1-coord-api, r1-docs, r1-downloads-cdn, plus Dockerfile.r1-browser) immediately after the source COPY lines — this gates every image build regardless of which trigger invokes it and requires no Cloud Build trigger changes. Note CGO: the tests pass with the modules' default settings, and the builder image is golang:1.25-bookworm so the toolchain is present. Optionally also add an explicit `test-services` step at the top of services/cloudbuild-deploy.yaml (golang:1.25, `for d in r1-admin r1-coord-api r1-docs r1-downloads-cdn; do (cd services/$d && go test ./... -count=1); done`) with the four build-* steps waitFor-ing it, so failures surface as a named CI step rather than inside docker build output.
confirmed.verify_reason: Split verdict — confirm the services half only. DESKTOP HALF REFUTED: the finder missed .github/workflows/desktop-augmentation.yml, which gates push-to-main and desktop/** / packages/web-components/** PRs with `cargo build --locked` + `cargo test --locked` on ubuntu/macos/windows, `npm test --workspace=@r1/web-components` (vitest), `npm test --workspace=desktop` (the r1d-*.test.ts files), and a 3-OS Playwright e2e job; web/ is additionally tested in root cloudbuild.yaml step web-build and .github/workflows/web.yml. The evidence sentence "no yaml references desktop/, cargo test, or vitest" is factually false. SERVICES HALF CONFIRMED with direct evidence: (1) `go list ./...` at repo root returns 0 services/ packages (five standalone go.mod modules), so the declared gate and cloudbuild.yaml:83/:95 `go test -mod=vendor ./...` never execute them; (2) services/cloudbuild-deploy.yaml:36-101 goes docker build → push → gcloud run deploy (push-to-main/staging/dev triggers, _ENV=prod) with only a /livez 200 smoke (lines 284-313), no test step; same for cloudbuild-r1-browser.yaml; (3) Dockerfiles COPY main_test.go (e.g. services/r1-coord-api/Dockerfile:7) but never RUN go test; (4) exhaustive grep of Makefile, scripts/, services/, .github/ finds no `go test` scoped to any services module (r1d-server.yml runs root-module `go vet ./...` only; bench-truthful-completion-pr.yaml tests root-module ./internal/bench); (5) the orphaned tests are real and currently green — all five modules pass locally, including security-relevant r1-coord-api/internal/auth (jwt/sso/middleware) and internal/tracking. Concrete consequence: an auth regression in r1-coord-api compiles, builds, and auto-deploys to prod with its own passing test suite never executed anywhere in CI.

confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at HEAD e88f48a7: no file outside internal/bridge imports the package (only pattern-mirror comments in internal/hub/builtin/coderadar_subscriber.go); all four constructors (cost.go:44, verify.go:21, wisdom.go:21, audit.go:20) are called only from internal/bridge/bridge_test.go; the six bridge event topics (bridge.go:16-21) are never published or subscribed anywhere else, and no supervisor rule pattern matches them, making doc.go:4-5 ('supervisor's rules subscribe to these events') false as well. confirmed.title: internal/harness: stance pipeline stops at bookkeeping — no stance runner exists, models.Provider is never called (mock is the only impl), and PauseStance can only time out
confirmed.evidence: SpawnStance (harness.go:54) builds a StanceSession with SystemPrompt/Model/AuthorizedTools, publishes bus.EvtWorkerSpawned, and returns — no goroutine, no model call, no tool loop is ever started. The `models.Provider` interface (internal/harness/models/provider.go:11) has exactly one implementation, MockProvider (models/mock.go), and `Chat` has ZERO call sites anywhere in the repo — grep 'models.Provider|models.Mock' outside internal/harness/models returns nothing. session.go:32 says 'CheckpointCheck should be called by the stance runner at safe points' but grep shows no stance runner exists: StanceCheckpointer/CheckpointCheck have no non-test callers outside internal/harness. Consequently PauseStance (harness.go:155) always hits `case <-time.After(30 * time.Second): return fmt.Errorf("harness: pause: stance %q did not acknowledge within 30s")` (harness.go:185) in any real use. The only production caller of SpawnStance is internal/bench/runner.go:177, which spawns a dev stance and immediately publishes mission.completed — the stance performs no work. TokensUsed/CostUSD on StanceSession are never written by anything.
confirmed.fix: Two proportionate options, either fixable in-repo. (A) Minimal activation: add a StanceRunner loop in internal/harness (new runner.go) that takes a StanceSession + models.Provider, drives Provider.Chat with the constructed SystemPrompt, enforces harness/tools authorization on returned ToolCalls, calls sess.CheckpointCheck between turns (making PauseStance/ResumeStance actually work), updates TokensUsed/CostUSD under h.mu, and emits worker.action.started/completed bus events; keep MockProvider for tests and add a thin adapter over the existing internal/provider clients as the first real Provider; have bench Runner.Run drive one runner turn so golden-mission metrics measure real substrate work. (B) Honest quarantine (smaller, fits an audit commit): delete internal/harness/models (zero importers), rewrite the harness.go:1-4 package comment and session.go:32 comment to say the execution runner is not yet built, and add an explicit 'Scoped: stance execution runner (harness substrate is lifecycle-bookkeeping only today)' entry to docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/FEATURE-MAP.md status sections, plus a specs/harness-activation.md stub following the governance-activation.md precedent. Option B is the correct audit-branch fix; option A belongs in a scoped activation spec.
confirmed.verify_reason: Every factual claim verifies at HEAD: SpawnStance (internal/harness/harness.go:54-150) does bookkeeping + bus publish only, no runner is started; internal/harness/models has ZERO importers repo-wide (stronger than claimed — even MockProvider and its tests are unused, the whole package is dead); session.go:32 references a 'stance runner' that does not exist (StanceCheckpointer/CheckpointCheck have only test callers, harness_test.go:139/147); PauseStance would time out at harness.go:185-186 absent a cooperating runner; TokensUsed/CostUSD (session.go:19-20) are never written so InspectStance (harness.go:303-304) always reports zeros; the sole non-test SpawnStance caller (internal/bench/runner.go:177) publishes mission.completed at line 194 with the stance having done nothing, and bench_test.go:242-245 asserts CostUSD==0/TokensUsed==0. Additional fact: bench.Runner.Run/RunAll have no non-test callers either (cmd/r1-bench uses NewRunner only for LoadMission/ListMissions), so the harness subsystem is entirely production-unreachable. Refutation attempts failed: no doc/spec marks the stance runner as scoped/future (FEATURE-MAP, ARCHITECTURE, specs/governance-activation.md all silent), yet harness.go:1-4 self-describes as 'the runtime layer that creates worker stances'. One overstatement in the claim: 'PauseStance can only time out in any real use' — there is no real use at all (no production caller), so no user currently experiences the 30s hang; this is dormant/incomplete substrate, not a live-path bug. confirmed.verify_reason: Verified at HEAD: skillmfr.New has zero callers outside internal/skillmfr/manufacturer_test.go (grep across repo), so Manufacturer.Start (manufacturer.go:43) never runs in production and no 'skill.' bus subscriber ever exists. confirmed.title: internal/remote: SessionReporter.Update is never called — 'live monitoring' pushes registration and final completion but zero progress snapshots

confirmed.fix: In cmd/r1/main.go runBuild, when reporter != nil, register a hub.ModeObserve subscriber on the existing eventBus (alongside hub.FlowTrackObserver) for EventTaskStarted/EventTaskCompleted/EventTaskFailed (and cost events if available). The subscriber maintains a mutex-guarded map[taskID]remote.TaskProgress plus running total cost, and pushes reporter.Update(remote.SessionUpdate{PlanID: cfg.PlanPath, Tasks: snapshot, TotalCostUSD: total}) from a single goroutine fed by a bounded channel (mirror internal/hub/builtin/analytics_subscriber.go's non-blocking pattern, since the reporter's HTTP client has a 10s timeout), throttled to at most 1 update/second with a final flush before Complete. Model the event-to-state translation on internal/server/bridge.go BridgeHubToDashboard. confirmed.title: specexec production wiring scores plan-only outcomes that carry no test/diff signal — winner degenerates to 'fastest plan' and the 0.9 early-stop threshold is mathematically unreachable
confirmed.evidence: The only production Run() wiring (scheduler.WithSpecExec, used by --specexec via cmd/r1/main.go:548,1499) forces every speculative strategy to PlanOnly=true ('CRITICAL: prevents execute/verify/merge', scheduler.go:452), so each Outcome has TestsPassed=TestsFailed=DiffLines=0. DefaultScorer (specexec.go:80-108) then awards the flat fallbacks: 0.3 (no test data) + 0.1 (no diff data) + up to 0.2 speed = max ~0.6 for every successful strategy, with duration the ONLY differentiator — the advertised 'Score results by test pass rate, code quality, diff size' (specexec.go:8) never applies. The spec sets EarlyStop:true, StopThreshold:0.9 (scheduler.go:435-436), which no plan-only outcome can reach (max 0.6), so early-stop is dead code in this wiring and 'pick the winner' silently means 'pick the plan that finished first'.
confirmed.fix: 1) Add PlanOutput string to scheduler.TaskResult (internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:17-28). 2) In cmd/r1/main.go execFn, when the workflow result has PlanOutput (plan-only mode), copy workflow Result.PlanOutput (workflow.go:190) into the returned scheduler.TaskResult. 3) In WithSpecExec's executor (scheduler.go:445-473), carry result.PlanOutput into the Outcome (add PlanText field to specexec.Outcome or reuse Artifacts/Insights) and replace DefaultScorer with a plan-aware Scorer for this wiring: deterministic structure scoring (non-empty plan, presence of concrete file paths verified against the repo, ordered steps, testable acceptance criteria — plan.Validate-style checks) so scores actually differentiate; optionally add a critic/rubric LLM pass behind the existing critic package. 4) Set StopThreshold to a value achievable under the new scorer (or set EarlyStop:false and delete StopThreshold from this wiring) so the early-stop path is either live or explicitly absent. 5) Update the WithSpecExec doc comment and specexec package doc to describe what is actually scored, and extend TestWithSpecExecSelectsWinner to assert that a higher-quality plan beats a faster-but-empty plan.
confirmed.verify_reason: Every factual element verified in the working tree. scheduler.WithSpecExec (the ONLY production caller of specexec.Run, wired at cmd/r1/main.go:547,1498 behind --specexec) forces PlanOnly=true (scheduler.go:449); the workflow plan-only branch (workflow.go:533-539) returns before verify/execute, so extractVerifyMetrics (main.go:6564-6582) yields TestsPassed=TestsFailed=DiffLines=0 for every speculative outcome. So prompt contextualization with SOW name/description is fully handled by an existing mechanism; the two fields are vestigial dead weight with a stale one-line comment. No user-visible behavior differs whether they are deleted or wired in (wiring would duplicate content already in prompts). This is a trivial cleanup nit (delete lines 217-219 and the two assignment lines), not partial wiring with a concrete consequence, so it does not meet the confirmation bar.

rejected.title: r1 mcp serve still never calls cortex.Start(): the 4 deterministic lobes it registers are permanently inert in the MCP daemon path
rejected.reason: The factual observation is correct (startMCPServer never calls Start), but the finding fails adversarial verification on three grounds. (1) The suggested fix is a no-op for the claimed problem: lobes run only when a Round is ticked (LobeRunner.run blocks on <-r.tick, internal/cortex/lobe.go:229-234), and the only production round driver is Cortex.MidturnNote (internal/cortex/cortex.go:541-557), invoked solely from the agentloop mid-turn hook. Nothing in internal/mcp/ or cmd/r1/ calls MidturnNote/TickRound (grep: zero hits), and the mcp.CortexBackend interface (internal/mcp/cortex_server.go:48-67) exposes no round trigger. Calling live.Start(ctx) would leave the 4 lobes exactly as inert — Start only spawns tick-blocked goroutines and a pre-warm pump that perpetually errors against stubProvider (mcp_serve_runtime.go:43-48), adding WARN/event noise for zero lobe activity. (2) The behavior is intentional, spec-documented design: specs/r1-mcp-serve.md D-2 (lines 106-116) states the ephemeral MCP cortex has "no Notes, no Lobe activity — but the handlers still work... lobes_list returns the registered defaults", and live attachment to a running session's cortex is explicitly deferred to a future --cortex-attach flag ("Out of scope here"). The spec's acceptance criteria (publish/notes round-trip, populated lobes_list) are all met without Start, and mcp_serve_runtime.go:69-76 honestly documents the not-Started state. (3) The surface where lobes are meant to run — the native loop — already Starts the cortex and drives rounds (internal/engine/native_runner.go:496-509); the MCP daemon is a workspace/registration inspection surface. No concrete user-visible consequence exists that the proposed fix would remedy; making MCP lobes live requires the spec'd future --cortex-attach or a new round-trigger tool, i.e., a feature request, not a half-closed wiring bug.

rejected.reason: Facts verified but the finding is refuted as intentional+documented design. All 12 specs (4 files) are indeed file-level skipped (desktop/tests/e2e/popout-lane.spec.ts:32, daemon-discovery.spec.ts:43, multi-session.spec.ts:31, lanes-streaming.spec.ts:30) and grep of desktop/src + desktop/src-tauri/src for test.windows.list / primary-window.closed / test.drive-lanes yields zero hits. The un-skip path is tracked as Layer B R1-DSK-1..11 in plans/PROGRAM-DAG-2026-05-15.md:58,287-326, explicitly deferred until 'after promotion is unblocked' — so 'no work since' is the plan operating as written, not a dormant system misrepresenting itself. The suggested fix is literally the Option A the repo rejected with documented rationale; re-litigating a documented tradeoff is a roadmap item, not a defect. Salvageable residue as a SEPARATE, smaller finding: docs overstate the state — docs/FEATURE-MAP.md:112 marks '4 Playwright e2e' as Done (with wrong path desktop/tests/agent/*.spec.ts; actual desktop/tests/e2e/), and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:568 + docs/BUSINESS-VALUE.md:168,174 count the 4 e2e specs in the test surface without disclosing all 12 are skipped. That is P3 docs-drift, not the test-gap as filed.

rejected.title: No CI lane runs `go test ./...` — nightly.yml claims twice that "PR CI continues to run go test ./..." but no workflow does
rejected.reason: The finder grepped only .github/ and missed that this repo's CI is Google Cloud Build, not GitHub Actions. cloudbuild.yaml (header line 2: "Replaces GitHub Actions ci.yml") runs the full gate: go build (line 46), go vet (line 54), go test -mod=vendor ./... -count=1 -timeout=120s (lines 75-85), and a -race lane (lines 87-97). scripts/setup-cloudbuild-base-ci-triggers.sh provisions both the push-to-main trigger (r1-agent-ci) and the pull-request trigger (r1-agent-pr, pattern ^.*$, lines 88-91) pointing at cloudbuild.yaml — so "PR CI" in nightly.yml refers to the Cloud Build PR lane, and its comment is accurate: that lane runs go test ./... without -tags integration, which skips the 1000-concurrent benchmark (Makefile:78), which is precisely why nightly.yml exists. The GHA-to-CloudBuild switch is intentional, documented design (commit a8838251 "ci: replace GHA with Cloud Build + local pre-push hook (#11)" — GHA disabled due to org billing suspension, scripts/pre-push.sh added as local mirror). The suggested fix would reintroduce the deliberately retired GHA lane. Whether the r1-agent-pr trigger is currently live in GCP is operator-side gcloud state, not verifiable or fixable in-repo (P3 ci-gap/BLOCKED at most); the finder's factual claim that no CI lane runs go test is wrong — cloudbuild.yaml:83 is that lane.

rejected.reason: The claim's premise is factually wrong. rejected.reason: The bait comments exist exactly as quoted (internal/promptguard/budget_test.go:148-155, internal/auth/bench_test.go:90, internal/tui/shell_test.go:12-17, internal/tui/lanes/lanes_render_test.go:61-64, internal/deploy/cloudflare/cloudflare_test.go:99-101, internal/chat/testing_stub.go:3-6), but the claim misreads the current working tree: the hook they game was decommissioned on 2026-05-20 (.claude/hooks/detect-stubs.sh.decommissioned-2026-05-20.bak) and no active enforcement greps those patterns. rejected.title: Bench CI-gate test weakens its own spec'd assertion to a t.Logf (terminal state)
rejected.reason: The finder reads lines 91-99 of /home/eric/repos/r1-agent/internal/bench/golden_test.go correctly (non-converged terminal state only t.Logf's in TestGoldenBaseline), but the claimed failure scenario cannot occur in the current tree. (1) The golden fixture directory internal/bench/testdata/missions/ contains exactly ONE mission, canonical-hello-world.json — there are no "other golden missions" that could stop converging silently. (2) That single mission IS hard-gated: TestGoldenNonRegression's baselines map (golden_test.go:130-136) pins TerminalState "converged" for it, and DetectRegression (internal/bench/compare.go:35) returns true whenever baseline converged and current did not, producing t.Errorf at golden_test.go:157. I ran `go test ./internal/bench/ -run 'TestGolden(Baseline|NonRegression)' -v`: both tests execute the mission for real (no skip path taken), it converges, and both PASS — so if canonical-hello-world stopped converging, CI would fail today via TestGoldenNonRegression. (3) The division of labor is intentional and documented in-file: golden_test.go:126-129 explicitly states "New canonical missions need an entry here to be regression-checked; anything not listed logs 'no baseline found, skipping regression check' but still runs the mission end-to-end for the baseline test above." Also note run errors are already t.Fatalf (classifyRunErr, lines 43-54), so a mission that errors out cannot pass silently either. What remains is a purely hypothetical future-mission gap (someone adds a fixture without a baselines entry), which is documented design, has no user-visible consequence in the current working tree, and per the verification rules ("failure scenario cannot actually occur" + "intentional+documented design") does not survive as a finding.

More importantly, the claim that the install path 'ships untested in every automated lane' misreads coverage: internal/serviceunit/service_test.go:96 (TestServiceUnit_InstallUninstallStatus) runs UN-GATED in go test ./... and drives the real kardianos Install/Status/Uninstall against the host service manager with a randomized unit name, asserting success => running/stopped and rejection => a recognized documented error. No concrete user-visible consequence was identified; prior audit scan-go-stubs.md:77 already triaged this as a known opt-in test gate, consistent with the repo's established pattern (R1_SERVER_UI_V2, playwright skips, R1_TEST_EMIT_FIXTURE).

rejected.title: bus.Subscription.Cancel never removes the subscription from Bus indexes — unbounded memory + publish-path growth
rejected.reason: The code reading is accurate (Cancel at internal/bus/bus.go:310-313 never removes the sub from b.subscribers/b.subIndex; only Close at bus.go:906-908 clears them; publishInternal rescans cancelled subs at bus.go:443-446), but the claimed failure scenario cannot occur in the current tree. The finder's named perpetrators are wrong: internal/bridge adapters contain zero Subscribe calls, and cmd/r1/descent_bus_bridge.go:128-131 subscribes once at startup and never Cancels (live intended subscriptions, not dead ones). Every production Cancel site is one-shot teardown immediately before Bus.Close or process exit: supervisor Stop (internal/supervisor/core.go:210,213) is only reached via governance.Governor.Close (internal/governance/governance.go:400-420), which closes its private per-mission bus in the same call; rulecheck lobe Run blocks on <-ctx.Done() (internal/cortex/lobes/rulecheck/lobe.go:131) so at most one subscription exists per runner lifetime, cancelled only at cortex shutdown on the per-process mcp-serve bus; skillmfr.Manufacturer has no production constructor caller (only skillmfr.NewRegistry is used); bench runner's bus is per-run with deferred Close. bus.New has exactly 3 production call sites and none cycles Subscribe/Cancel on a live bus. No unbounded accumulation, no publish-path degradation, no user-visible consequence at HEAD — at most a latent API-hygiene hazard (optional one-line hardening mirroring RemoveHook's index removal at bus.go:733-752) that does not meet the confirm bar.

rejected.title: EvtBusSubscriberOverflow / EvtBusHookInjectionFailed have active subscribers but are never published
rejected.reason: The finding's factual core (events declared at bus.go:101/103 but never published; overflow path bus.go:672-678 and injected-failure path bus.go:386-390 only log) is accurate, but its load-bearing evidence misreads the code. None of the three cited "production consumers expecting these types" would do anything if the events were published: (1) cmd/r1/descent_bus_bridge.go lists them in the descentSubtypeFor branch that explicitly returns ("", false) — "Non-descent events have no streamjson subtype mapping" — and the bridge subscribes only to bus.DescentEventKinds patterns (lines 129-131), so it can never receive bus.* events at all; the severity listing at 109-110 is unreachable for these types. (2) harness.go:382-383 is inside Recover's Replay filtered to Pattern{TypePrefix: "worker."} (line 336) — bus.* events can never match — and the branch comment says "not relevant to stance replay; ignore." (3) supervisor/core.go:182-183 is an explicit "do not trigger a supervisor checkpoint" no-op branch. The claimed user-visible consequence ("observability surfaces built to report exactly that condition receive nothing") therefore cannot occur — no such surface exists; even the sibling events that ARE published (EvtBusHandlerPanic, EvtBusHookActionFailed) have no functional consumers beyond WAL persistence. Overflow tracking via in-memory counter is documented as intentional at bus.go:339 ("tracks subscriber overflow events for testing"). What survives is a P3 nit: two dead constants and a stale comment at internal/supervisor/hooks.go:18-19 falsely claiming the bus surfaces `bus.evt_hook_injection_failed` — not the claimed partial-wiring defect.

rejected.title: session.SQLStore.SaveLearning runs DELETE + row-by-row INSERT without a transaction — mid-failure destroys all learned patterns
rejected.reason: The code text matches the claim (sqlstore.go:205 DELETE + 208-212 bare INSERT loop, no transaction), but the failure scenario cannot occur: SQLStore.SaveLearning has zero call sites anywhere in the repo. cmd/r1/main.go:4140/4187 and integration_test.go:577 call only LoadLearning; store_test.go:50 exercises the JSON Store's SaveLearning (atomic writeJSON to learning.json, store.go:158-160), not the SQLStore. The only production writer to the SQLite patterns table is SaveAttempt -> addPattern (sqlstore.go:162-169, 200-202), a single-statement INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upsert that is atomic and never deletes rows. Since the DELETE never executes on any code path, the claimed 'permanent loss of cross-task learning data' is unreachable. The method exists only to satisfy the SessionStore interface (store.go:26); the real residual issue is dormant/unhardened code, not the claimed data-destruction bug.

rejected.title: wisdom.SQLiteStore.Record silently drops learnings when the INSERT fails
rejected.reason: The code reading is textually correct (sqlite.go:182-186 discards the Exec error; Learnings() returns nil on rows.Err() at 213-215), but the claimed failure scenario cannot occur. (1) The headline STOKE_DB_ENCRYPTION wrong-key scenario fails loudly at open, not silently at Record: NewSQLiteStore's schema Exec at sqlite.go:154 errors through sqlite3mc ("file is not a database") and the constructor returns an error fail-closed (documented at sqlite.go:31-33), so no store exists to drop learnings. (2) The consequence "every learning recorded during a session vanishes; the caller believes cross-task learning is accumulating" is unreachable: repo-wide grep shows wisdom.NewSQLiteStore/SQLiteStore have ZERO callers outside internal/wisdom's own tests. All production wisdom paths use the in-memory *wisdom.Store (cmd/r1/main.go:291,1447,3004; LoadWisdom JSON snapshots at cmd/r1/sow_wisdom.go:198; bridge/wisdom.go:15; internal/mcp/memory.go:21; memoryrecall.NewMemoryRecallLobe takes *wisdom.Store at cmd/r1/mcp_serve_runtime.go:119 and internal/engine/native_runner.go:627). (3) The void Record signature is intentional documented parity with the infallible in-memory Store.Record (sqlite.go:132-133 "satisfies the same API as Store for drop-in replacement"; wisdom.go:78-86 is an append that cannot fail). No concrete user-visible consequence exists today. The residual truth is a different finding than claimed: wisdom.SQLiteStore is dormant/unwired code (P3 dead-code observation), and a log line on Exec/rows.Err would be cheap hygiene if that code is ever wired — but the bug as stated (silent session data loss) is refuted.

rejected.title: Descent-evidence drawer claims the host lacks descent evidence IPC, but descent_tier_history with evidence_ref is registered
rejected.reason: The finder traced only the Tauri layer and stopped. Yes, ipc.rs registers `descent_tier_history` (desktop/src-tauri/src/ipc.rs:581, impl :403-416) and DescentAttempt carries `evidence_ref` (:378) — but that command is a pure pass-through: it calls `mgr.rpc_call(session_id, "descent.tier_history", ...)`, which round-trips to the spawned `r1 desktop-rpc` subprocess (desktop/src-tauri/src/subprocess.rs:148-161). That server's handler is hardwired to the scaffold stub: `handler: &desktopapi.NotImplemented{}` (cmd/r1/desktop_rpc_cmd.go:85), and `NotImplemented.DescentTierHistory` returns `ErrNotImplemented` (internal/desktopapi/desktopapi.go:406-408). A repo-wide grep confirms NotImplemented is the ONLY implementation of DescentTierHistory/DescentCurrentTier — no real descent data source is wired anywhere. So the claimed failure scenario cannot occur: calling descent_tier_history from openDrawer would never yield attempts or evidence_ref; it would return an RPC not_implemented error, and the drawer would have to render an unavailable state — exactly what it renders now, minus a wasted round-trip. The user-visible copy "evidence for <tier> cannot be queried here" is factually TRUE of the current host stack end-to-end. It is also intentional, documented design: descent-evidence.ts:6-9 states the drawer "renders an explicit unavailable state instead of fabricating evidence rows," and desktopapi.go:345-347 documents the NotImplemented scaffold as the R1D-1 phase plan ("swap in real method bodies one verb at a time across later R1D-* phases"). The suggested fix produces zero user-visible improvement until someone implements Handler.DescentTierHistory in the Go backend — a separate, much larger feature that belongs to that phase's scope. Not partial wiring in the panel; the panel is honest about a backend that genuinely is not implemented.
